v2:8b75ad1458fd1984d8cc2bfdf25e61f86b059.summary: Verified against live docs on 2026-09-02: all four Anthropic models (Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5), OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, and Gemini 3.7 Flash / 3.1 Pro Preview accept image input and support strict JSON-schema structured outputs, so the choice is driven by vision quality, reliability, latency, cost and API ergonomics rather than capability gaps. Recommendation: primary `claude-opus-5` (Anthropic's own "start here" model, explicitly positioned for vision-heavy workflows, high-res 2576px vision tier, GA structured outputs via `output_config.format` + `messages.parse`, $5/$25 per MTok, 1000 RPM / 2M ITPM even at Start tier) with `claude-sonnet-5` ($2/$10, "Fast", same API surface, no safety-classifier refusals) as the drop-in fallback and as the model for the cheap vision-observation and critic stages. Do not use Fable 5.1 for this: 2x price, "Slower", forced `tool_choice` returns 400, 30-day data retention required, smaller rate-limit bucket (500K ITPM / 100K OTPM at Start), and its vision uplift comes mostly from a crop/zoom tool that also lifts Opus/Sonnet. GPT-5.6 Sol (`gpt-5.6-sol`, $4/$20) is a close second and Gemini 3.7 Flash (`gemini-3.7-flash`, $0.75/$3.75 promo, ~340 tok/s) is the cheapest/fastest option, but Google's Pro flagship is still `-preview` and the Flash promo price ends 2026-12-31. Pipeline: pre-resize image in code -> vision observation (structured, with a `zoom` crop tool) -> deterministic template routing -> rulebook-grounded generation of a base size only (cached system prompt) -> compute grading/derived measurements/colorway matrix in code -> schema + code validators -> LLM critic -> bounded (max 2) repair loop. SO-Bench shows frontier models hit ~97% schema validity but <12% exact-value match on image->JSON, which is the empirical case for computing every number you can in code. SDK: TypeScript `@anthropic-ai/sdk` (0.123.0) with Zod `zodOutputFormat` if the demo is a Node/Next.js web app; Python `anthropic` 1.x with Pydantic `messages.parse` otherwise. Env var: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

findings.topic: Anthropic current lineup, IDs, limits, pricing (live docs)
findings.detail: Claude Fable 5.1 `claude-fable-5-1` (released 2026-09-01): 1M ctx, 128K out, $10/$50, latency 'Slower', thinking always-on, cache read $0.25. Claude Opus 5 `claude-opus-5`: 1M ctx, 128K out, $5/$25, 'Moderate', adaptive thinking on by default, cache read $0.50, 5m cache write $6.25. Claude Sonnet 5 `claude-sonnet-5` (released 2026-06-30): 1M ctx, 128K out, $2/$10 (introductory price made permanent; the planned Sept 1 increase to $3/$15 was cancelled), 'Fast', cache read $0.20. Claude Haiku 4.5 `claude-haiku-4-5` (alias of `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`): 200K ctx, 64K out, $1/$5, 'Fastest', old extended-thinking API (budget_tokens), no effort param, knowledge cutoff Feb 2025. All four: text+image in, text out. Batch API = 50% off. Docs say 'start with Claude Opus 5 for most workloads'. Model IDs are dateless pinned snapshots; never append date suffixes.

findings.topic: Anthropic structured outputs (GA) - exactly what this pipeline needs
findings.detail: `output_config: {format: {type: 'json_schema', schema}}` on messages.create (old `output_format` param and beta header `structured-outputs-2025-11-13` are gone). Supported on Fable 5.1/5, Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6/4.5, Sonnet 5/4.6/4.5, Haiku 4.5, on Claude API + Bedrock + Vertex + Foundry. SDK helpers: Python `client.messages.parse(..., output_format=PydanticModel)` -> `.parsed_output`; TS `client.messages.parse` + `zodOutputFormat()` from `@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/zod` (or `jsonSchemaOutputFormat`). Strict tool use: `strict: true` on the tool (schema must have `additionalProperties:false` + `required`). Schema limits that matter for a tech pack: NO `minimum`/`maximum`/`multipleOf`, NO `minLength`/`maxLength`, NO recursive schemas, `minItems` only 0 or 1, enums only primitives, `additionalProperties` only false; `$ref`/`$defs` OK. First request per schema pays a grammar-compile latency (cached 24h); changing the format invalidates the prompt cache; format is incompatible with citations.

findings.topic: Anthropic vision limits and image token cost
findings.detail: Image sources: base64, URL, or Files API `file_id`. Formats JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP; 10 MB per image on Claude API (5 MB on Bedrock/Vertex); 32 MB request cap; up to 600 images/request on 1M models. Token cost = ceil(w/28)*ceil(h/28) visual tokens. High-res tier (Claude 4.7 and later = Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5): max long edge 2576 px, max 4784 tokens; Haiku 4.5 is standard tier (1568 px / 1568 tokens). A 1000x1000 product photo = 1296 tokens (~$0.0065 on Opus 5, ~$0.0026 on Sonnet 5); a 3840x2160 photo = 4784 tokens on hi-res models. Put images BEFORE text in the user turn. Claude may mis-count small objects and coordinates are approximate - do not rely on it for measurement extraction from a photo.

findings.topic: Crop/zoom tool is the single biggest vision uplift (and works on Opus/Sonnet, not just Fable)
findings.detail: Anthropic's cookbook `zoom` tool (inputs x1,y1,x2,y2,image_index; returns a JPEG crop scaled to the 2576px/4784-token budget) raised Chartography accuracy from 29%->73% on claude-fable-5 and 13%->44% on claude-sonnet-5. The Fable 5.1 prompting guide says the same: give vision work a crop tool; a container with PIL/OpenCV is optional. Cost trade-off: ~10x more tokens per question when the tool is used. For a bucket-hat photo, use it to verify brim topstitch rows, eyelets, label placement, and seam type.

findings.topic: Why NOT Fable 5.1 as primary for this prototype
findings.detail: (1) 2x Opus price ($10/$50) with 'Slower' latency; single hard requests can run minutes. (2) `tool_choice: any`/`tool` returns 400 on Fable 5.1 - forced tool calls are a common structured-output pattern. (3) Requires 30-day data retention (ZDR orgs get 400). (4) Smaller rate-limit bucket: Start tier 1,000 RPM / 500K ITPM / 100K OTPM (Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 get 2M ITPM / 400K OTPM), and Fable 5 + 5.1 share it. (5) Safety classifiers can return stop_reason 'refusal'. (6) Anthropic's own guidance: use Fable 5.1 only 'when your evals on Claude Opus 5 at higher effort still fall short'. Its raw vision gain is real but the crop tool delivers most of the uplift on cheaper models. Re-evaluate later at `effort: low` where docs claim it is cost-competitive with Opus/Sonnet.

findings.topic: Opus 5 specifics relevant to the build
findings.detail: Thinking on by default (adaptive); control cost with `output_config.effort` (low/medium/high/xhigh/max; default high). Disabling thinking is allowed only at effort<=high and causes tool calls to leak into text - keep thinking on and lower effort instead. Sampling params (temperature/top_p/top_k) are rejected on Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 (400) - determinism comes from schema + effort + code, not temperature. Docs list 'Vision: understanding charts, documents, diagrams... strongest when given tools to iteratively analyze, crop, and verify' among Opus 5's largest gains, and the selection matrix names 'vision-heavy workflows' for Opus 5 and 'visual understanding' for Sonnet 5. Minimum cacheable prompt on Opus 5 is 512 tokens. Opus 5 has refusal classifiers: add `fallbacks: 'default'` + beta `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` (Claude API only; use SDK `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` on Bedrock/Vertex). Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 are not listed as having classifier refusals.

findings.topic: Anthropic rate limits and spend caps for a startup demo
findings.detail: Start tier: Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Haiku 4.5 = 1,000 RPM, 2,000,000 ITPM, 400,000 OTPM each (separate buckets per model); monthly spend cap $500 (Build $1,000; Scale $200,000). Cached input tokens do NOT count toward ITPM. New orgs may begin in an 'Evaluation' tier with lower limits until history builds - buy credits and run traffic a week before demo day. Hitting the spend cap returns 429 with error_code `enforced_spend_limit_reached` and no retry-after.

findings.topic: Anthropic Files API (GA, no beta header)
findings.detail: `client.files.upload(...)` -> `file_id`, referenced as `{type:'image', source:{type:'file', file_id}}`. 500 MB/file, 1 TB/org, ~500 file requests/min, optional `expires_in_seconds` (3,600-7,776,000). Files are workspace-scoped (any key in the workspace can read them) - never accept file_ids from end users; keep the user->file mapping in your app DB. Not available on Bedrock/Vertex. Useful here so the photo is uploaded once and referenced by every pipeline stage instead of re-sending base64. Needs Python SDK >=1.2.0 / TS SDK >=0.122.0 for the non-beta namespace.

GPT-5.6 launched 2026-07-09 as Sol/Terra/Luna. Official model page: `gpt-5.6-sol` (alias `gpt-5.6`) $4 in / $0.40 cached / $20 out per 1M (third-party trackers still show $5/$30 pre-Aug-21; OpenAI cut Sol >20% on 2026-08-21 - treat $4/$20 as promotional and re-check), `gpt-5.6-terra` $2/$12, `gpt-5.6-luna` $0.20/$1.20. All: 1,050,000 ctx, 128K out, text+image in, structured outputs + function calling, reasoning.effort none/low/medium(default)/high/xhigh/max, knowledge cutoff 2026-02-16; >272K-token prompts billed 2x input/1.5x output. Tier 1 limits 500 RPM / 500K TPM. Previous: `gpt-5.5` ($5/$30, snapshot gpt-5.5-2026-04-23), `gpt-5.4` ($2.50/$15). Structured outputs via Responses API `text.format: {type:'json_schema', strict:true}`; SDK helpers `client.responses.parse` (Pydantic) and `zodTextFormat` (Zod); refusals come back as a `refusal` content item. Env var `OPENAI_API_KEY`; npm `openai` 7.9.0.

Current stable: `gemini-3.7-flash` (Aug 2026; 1,048,576 in / 65,536 out; text, image, video, audio, PDF in; thinking low/medium/high; structured output + function calling), `gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash` ($1.50/$9), `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` ($0.30/$2.50). Image tokens: 258 per 768x768 tile (258 flat if <=384px), `media_resolution` controls the per-image token cap; up to 3,600 images/request; inline data capped at 20 MB. Structured output supports `minimum`/`maximum`/`minItems`/`maxItems` (which Anthropic rejects). SDKs: Python `google-genai`, JS `@google/genai` 2.20.0; env var `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Artificial Analysis: Gemini 3.7 Flash ~340 tok/s, TTFT 0.77 s.

Artificial Analysis: Claude Sonnet 5 at max-effort adaptive reasoning streams ~69-79 tok/s with TTFT measured in the tens-to-hundreds of seconds because thinking precedes the first visible token; Gemini 3.7 Flash (low) TTFT 0.77 s at ~340 tok/s; GPT-5.6 Terra non-reasoning TTFT 1.33 s. Implication for the demo: run Claude stages at `effort: medium` (vision observation, critic) and `high` (generation), always stream (`messages.stream().finalMessage()`), show per-stage progress in the UI, and budget 30-90 s end-to-end for the full multi-stage pipeline.

findings.topic: Empirical evidence for image->JSON failure modes (SO-Bench)
findings.detail: SO-Bench (~1,800 image samples, 6,500 schemas across UI/natural/document/chart): frontier models reach ~96-98% JSON-schema validity but only 5-11% exact full-structure match (Gemini 2.5 Pro 97.7% valid / 11.4% exact; GPT-5 96.4% / 5.2%). Dominant errors: shallow structures on deep schemas, hallucinated extra fields, misread numbers/units. Schema-guided prompting (spelling out enum values and constraints in the prompt, since the grammar cannot enforce numeric ranges) measurably helps. Conclusion for a tech pack: never let the model produce graded measurements or derived numbers - only base-size observations and qualitative fields; compute the rest.

findings.topic: Anthropic's workflow patterns applied to this pipeline
findings.detail: 'Building effective agents': prefer prompt chaining with programmatic gates between steps when the task decomposes into fixed subtasks (it does here); evaluator-optimizer only 'when we have clear evaluation criteria and iterative refinement provides measurable value' - use it as a bounded critic->repair step, not an open agent loop. Production write-ups (Alan) confirm: Pydantic/Zod validation, structured validation errors fed back to the model, bounded retries (<=2-3), and human review on persistent failure.

S0 code: normalize image (long edge <=1568 px to cap at ~1.5K tokens, JPEG q85, strip EXIF), hash, optional Files API upload. S1 Opus 5 (effort medium) 'VisionObservations' via output_config.format: category enum (bucket_hat/cap/...), panel count, brim type, topstitch rows, closures, eyelets, colors as approximate hex + confidence, fabric appearance, reversible {yes/no/unknown}; provide the `zoom` strict tool for detail checks. S2 code: merge user text (authoritative) over observations; select template `bucket_hat_reversible`; unresolved fields -> clarifying-question list. S3 Opus 5 (effort high) 'TechPackDraft' with a cached rulebook system prompt (hat size table, seam/stitch catalogue ASTM D6193 stitch 301/401/504, thread Tex 27-40, SPI 8-10 for 280 gsm twill, seam allowances 1.0 cm, reversible-construction rules: enclosed/bound seams, no exposed allowances, two BOM lines per shell) + one few-shot exemplar; instruct 'base size M only, no grading'. S4 code: grade S/L from M (head circumference S 56 / M 58 / L 60 cm, +/-0.5 cm tol; crown depth ~9.0-9.5 cm; brim 6-7 cm; crown circumference = head + 1.0-1.5 cm ease), colorway matrix (2 colorways x 2 faces), consumption, hex/unit regex checks. S5 code validators (JSON schema, monotonic sizes, unit sanity) then Sonnet 5 (effort low) 'CritiqueReport' {issues[{path,severity,fix}]}. S6 bounded repair (max 2): send JSON + issues, request patched JSON via structured output, re-run S5. Log every stage with usage for evals.
findings.source: industry knowledge; size data from https://www.solbari.com/pages/technical-bucket-hat-size-guide and https://www.solbari.com/pages/go-to-bucket-hat-men-size-guide

findings.topic: Tool-use vs output_config.format for structured output
findings.detail: Use `output_config.format` + `messages.parse()` for the single-document outputs (observations, draft, critique) - it is grammar-enforced and returns a parsed object. Use `strict: true` tools only where the model must act (the `zoom` crop tool). Do not rely on `tool_choice: {type:'tool'}` to force JSON - it is removed on Fable 5.1 and unnecessary elsewhere. Keep schemas flat-ish (no recursion, no numeric ranges - encode ranges as enums or validate in code), put the strict enums in the prompt text as well (SO-Bench finding), and keep the schema byte-stable so the compiled grammar (24h cache) and the prompt cache both hit. Parse tool inputs with JSON.parse/json.loads - never string-match.

findings.topic: Prompt caching setup for the rulebook
findings.detail: Render order tools -> system -> messages; put the frozen rulebook + exemplar + schema instructions first in `system` with `cache_control: {type:'ephemeral'}` (5-min write 1.25x, read 0.1x; 1-hour write 2x). Opus 5 minimum cacheable prefix 512 tokens. Any byte change (timestamps, per-request IDs, reordered enums, a changed output_config.format) invalidates the cache; verify `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` > 0 on the second call. Cache reads also do not count toward ITPM rate limits.

Assume 1.3K image tokens + ~3K prompt in / 1.5K out (S1), ~8K in mostly cached / 4K out incl. thinking (S3), ~6K in / 1K out (S5), one repair ~7K in / 3K out. All on Opus 5: ~$0.10-0.15 input + $0.20-0.30 output = roughly $0.30-0.50 per pack (thinking tokens are billed as output). Opus 5 for S1+S3 and Sonnet 5 for S5/S6: ~$0.25-0.40. All Sonnet 5: ~$0.12-0.20. All Fable 5.1: ~$0.60-1.20. GPT-5.6 Sol at $4/$20 lands ~$0.25-0.40; Gemini 3.7 Flash ~$0.03-0.06. Batch API halves Claude cost but is unsuitable for an interactive demo.
findings.source: industry knowledge (derived from the official price tables cited above)

findings.detail: TypeScript: `npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk` (0.123.0 on npm as of today) + `zod`; `const client = new Anthropic()` (reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); `client.messages.parse({model:'claude-opus-5', max_tokens:16000, output_config:{format: zodOutputFormat(TechPackSchema), effort:'high'}, messages:[...]})` -> `response.parsed_output`; for long outputs `client.messages.stream(...).finalMessage()`; timeouts are in milliseconds. Python: `pip install anthropic` (1.x, Python >=3.10, httpx2); `client.messages.parse(..., output_format=TechPack)`; timeouts in seconds. Pick TypeScript if the demo is a Next.js/Node web app on the marketplace stack; Python if the team wants Pydantic + Pillow/OpenCV for the crop tool and post-processing (S0/S4) in one process. Both SDKs auto-retry 408/409/429/5xx twice. Use typed errors (RateLimitError etc.) and check `stop_reason` ('refusal', 'max_tokens') before reading content.

Anthropic: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (credential resolution order: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -> `ant auth login` profile -> WIF env vars); optional `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. OpenAI: `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Google: `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Keep them in `.env` (never in the repo), one provider adapter interface so GPT-5.6 / Gemini can be A/B-tested behind the same `TechPackSchema`. Claude on Bedrock/Vertex uses `AnthropicBedrockMantle` / `AnthropicVertex` clients with cloud credentials instead of an Anthropic key (but no Files API, no server-side fallbacks, 5 MB image cap there).
findings.source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision (curl examples use $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output ($GEMINI_API_KEY), industry knowledge for OPENAI_API_KEY

recommendations: Primary model: `claude-opus-5` for the vision-observation (effort `medium`) and generation (effort `high`) stages; fallback and cheap-stage model: `claude-sonnet-5` (critic/repair at effort `low`, and full pipeline fallback on Opus 429/refusal). Reserve `claude-haiku-4-5` only for trivial enum classification if you need it; skip `claude-fable-5-1` for the prototype and re-benchmark it later at `effort: low` once you have an eval set.

Use the Anthropic SDK directly (TypeScript `@anthropic-ai/sdk` + Zod `zodOutputFormat` for a Node/Next.js demo; Python `anthropic` 1.x + Pydantic if post-processing/crop tooling lives in Python). Use `client.messages.parse` with `output_config.format` for every document-shaped output, `strict: true` only for the `zoom` crop tool, and `messages.stream().finalMessage()` for the generation stage.

Enable `fallbacks: 'default'` with beta header `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` on Opus 5 calls so classifier refusals auto-retry on Anthropic's recommended model; always branch on `stop_reason` before reading content.

Build the pipeline as prompt chaining with code gates: (0) resize/normalize image in code -> (1) structured VisionObservations with zoom tool -> (2) deterministic merge with user text + template routing -> (3) rulebook-grounded TechPackDraft for base size M only, rulebook + exemplar cached with `cache_control` -> (4) compute grading (S 56 / M 58 / L 60 cm head circ, +/-0.5 cm), derived measurements, colorway matrix and BOM consumption in code -> (5) JSON-schema + business-rule validators, then a Sonnet 5 CritiqueReport -> (6) at most 2 repair iterations, then human review flag.

Design the JSON schemas around Anthropic's grammar limits: no numeric min/max, no minLength/maxLength, no recursion; encode allowed values as enums (size codes, stitch types 301/401/504, SPI 8|9|10, Tex 27|40|60, seam classes) and repeat the enums in prompt text; keep the schema byte-stable across requests so grammar and prompt caches hit.

Pre-resize photos to <=1568 px long edge (about 1.3-1.5K visual tokens) for the first pass; let the zoom tool pull full-resolution crops only for details (topstitch rows, eyelets, labels). Upload once via the Files API and reference by file_id across stages; keep the user->file_id mapping server-side.

Before the demo: purchase Anthropic credits so the org leaves the Evaluation tier, confirm Start-tier limits (1,000 RPM / 2M ITPM / 400K OTPM per model, $500/month cap), run 20-30 warm-up generations to prime prompt caches and surface refusals, and log usage per stage to validate the ~$0.30-0.50 per-pack estimate.

Wrap providers behind one adapter so `gpt-5.6-sol` (Responses API, `text.format` json_schema strict, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) and `gemini-3.7-flash` (`response_json_schema`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) can be A/B-tested on the same eval set; Gemini 3.7 Flash is the obvious candidate if per-pack cost or sub-second TTFT later matters more than quality.

Create a 15-30 item eval set now (reversible bucket hat variants, sketches vs photos, Arabic/English descriptions, missing info) with expected observations and measurement tables, and use it to sweep effort levels per stage (Anthropic's guidance: effort is a better lever than switching models).
open_questions: Is the prototype a Node/Next.js web app (favors TypeScript SDK + Zod) or a Python service (favors Pydantic + Pillow/OpenCV for the crop tool and post-processing)?
Does the org already have an Anthropic Console account with purchased credits, and which usage tier is it on? (Evaluation-tier limits could break a live demo.)

What is the acceptable end-to-end latency for the demo (e.g. under 60 s with streamed progress vs. several minutes offline)? This decides effort levels and whether the critic/repair loop runs synchronously.
Target cost per generated tech pack and expected demo/beta volume? (Determines whether Opus 5 everywhere, Opus+Sonnet split, or Gemini Flash for some stages.)

Do you have 1-3 real factory-approved tech packs (ideally from Egyptian suppliers) to use as few-shot exemplars and to define the measurement/POM naming conventions the factory expects (cm vs inches, half-measure vs full circumference)?
Must outputs be bilingual (Arabic + English) and/or exported to PDF/Excel? (Affects schema design and whether a rendering stage is needed.)
Is US-only inference / data residency (`inference_geo: 'us'`, 1.1x price) or use of Bedrock/Vertex required for compliance, which would drop Files API and server-side fallbacks?

Should the pipeline accept multiple images per product (front/back/detail) and hand sketches, and how should conflicts between the photo and the text description be resolved (text wins, ask user, or flag)?

v2:8c8d808d1fc448c5a8d0bc72186c46110cb3d.summary: A factory-ready apparel/accessory tech pack is a versioned document whose canonical order is: cover/header -> technical flats with callouts -> BOM -> measurement (POM) chart with base size, grade rules and tolerances -> construction/workmanship (ISO 4915 stitch, ISO 4916 seam, SPI, seam allowance, topstitch, pressing) -> colorways / BOM-by-color -> labels, packing and QC/AQL -> fit comments and revision log (sources: Techpacker, Apparel Entrepreneurship, Sewport, Fashion Index, Specter OS headwear guide). For the canonical bucket-hat case the industry numbers are concrete: EN 13402-style head girth S 55-56 / M 57-58 / L 59-60 cm with 1 cm ease and 1-2 cm grade, crown depth 8-10 cm, brim 5-7 cm, 1 cm seam allowance, 301 lockstitch at 10-12 SPI seaming and 7-8 SPI topstitch, Tex 40 poly-core topstitch / Tex 27-30 seaming, tolerances +/-0.5 cm on crown/brim and +/-1.0 cm on circumference, AQL 2.5 major / 4.0 minor at ISO 2859-1 GII. Egypt's domestic market requires Arabic labels (country of origin, manufacturer name, product description) and the mandatory ES 7266 series (7266-3/2023 apparel & home textiles, 7266-4 garments) covering fiber content %, care (ES 1405/2014 = ISO 3758 symbols), origin, manufacturer/importer and restricted chemicals; export markets add EU 1007/2011 fiber naming, US FTC fiber/origin/RN + 16 CFR 423 care, and GSO/SASO Arabic fiber+care+origin. For a prototype, the MUST set is header, front/back/side flat with callouts, BOM with composition/gsm/width/consumption/color ref, POM chart across 3 sizes with cm tolerances, construction notes with stitch/SPI/SA/thread, colorway table with Pantone TCX, label list and packing basics; costing, grading formulas, detailed carton specs and sample-stage sign-off can be NICE placeholders.

findings.detail: Techpacker's 2026 guide: (1) cover/style info, (2) technical flat sketches front/back/side with callouts to every seam, stitch detail and hardware, (3) BOM with Pantone color ref, supplier ref, unit of measure, (4) POM chart at base size with tolerance per POM + grading rules, (5) construction notes (seam types, SPI, thread color, finishing), (6) cost sheet, (7) revision history. Apparel Entrepreneurship's 10-page order: cover, front/back flats, detail flats, measurement spec, BOM, construction & workmanship, colorways, graphics/embroidery, labels & packaging, fit comments & revision log. Specter OS headwear-specific order: cover (style, season, colourway, revision history), flats (front/back/side/detail), BOM, POM, construction (stitch types, seam allowances), decoration specs, colourways, labelling & packaging. Sewport's five measurement columns: POM, Description (how to measure), Requested, Tolerance +/-, Fit comments.

Union of sources: brand, style name, style number, season/drop, product category, gender, fit type, sample (base) size and size range, colorway list, date created, last modified, version number, designer/technical designer, fit approver / approval sign-off, factory name, country of origin, target retail/FOB price, thumbnail flat. Techpacker: style name, style number, season, colorways, brand, date, version. Fashinza/WFX product summary adds product code, product type, gender, creation date, last modified, country of origin, retail price. Revision log must record what changed, when, who approved.

Black-and-white vector flats, no color/shading, front and back minimum; side and interior/inside-out views for accessories and reversibles; separate detail/zoom flats with cross-sections for construction layers; callout lines to every seam, topstitch row, label placement, hardware; POM letters drawn on a dedicated POM sketch so each measurement code maps to a line on the drawing. For the reversible bucket hat: front, side, top (crown tip), inside-out view of reverse colorway, brim cross-section showing the 2-layer sandwich and topstitch position.

Recommended columns: item no.; component/placement (e.g. outer shell, reverse shell, brim, thread, main label); description; material type; fiber composition; construction (3/1 twill); weight gsm (with +/-5% tolerance); width cm (usable); finish (pre-shrunk, peached, enzyme); supplier + article/reference no.; color name + Pantone TCX + lab-dip ref; consumption per unit (m, pcs) and wastage %; unit of measure; size dependency (Y/N, per-size values); comments/test requirements (shrinkage <=3%, colorfastness ISO 105-C06 grade 4). Sewport lists: Placement, Comments, Material (fiber content, ID numbers), Supplier, Colour Number. Techpacker: color ref (Pantone), supplier ref, UoM. AE: main fabric content, weight, width, finish; lining/interlining; trims with codes; labels; thread; packaging.

findings.topic: Main fabric spec for the canonical case
findings.detail: 100% cotton 3/1 twill, 280 gsm +/-5%, 145-150 cm cuttable width, pre-shrunk (residual shrinkage <=3% at 60 C wash), yarn-dyed or piece-dyed; two shells required (khaki + black) since the hat is reversible. Consumption: DIY patterns quote ~0.5 m of 112 cm fabric per shell; on a 150 cm marker an adult bucket hat (crown tip, 2 side-band pieces, 2 brim pieces) typically nests at ~0.25-0.30 m per shell, so plan ~0.28 m khaki + ~0.28 m black per hat plus 8-10% wastage for a first run (marker-yield number is an estimate, confirm with factory).

findings.topic: Trims: thread, labels, hangtags, polybags, cartons
findings.detail: Thread: headwear standard is Tex 40 polyester (poly-core or spun) tonal for seams and topstitch (Specter OS); A&E woven guide uses T-24/T-27 for seaming/loopers and T-40 core for topstitch on casual pants; needle Nm 80-90 (80/12-90/14) for Tex 27-40. For 280 gsm twill: seaming Tex 27-30 with Nm 80-90 needle; brim topstitch Tex 40 (Tex 60 if a heavier decorative look) with Nm 90-100. Labels: main/brand woven label (~30x40 mm) at centre back inside crown; size label below main label; care+content label (fiber %, care symbols, origin, manufacturer); country-of-origin. For a reversible hat the label goes into the side-band/brim seam so it reads from either side, or use printed/heat-transfer labels on the inner reverse. Hangtag: card weight, string/plastic tag-pin, attachment point (brim edge or label). Polybag: clear PE with suffocation warning, size and thickness (typ. 0.03-0.04 mm), one hat per bag flat or nested. Carton: 5-ply corrugated, inner/master ratio, size assortment, gross weight max (<=15-18 kg typical buyer rule), carton marks: style, PO, colour, size, qty, carton no./total, origin, gross/net weight, dimensions.

findings.topic: POM conventions, codes, base size, grade rules, tolerances
findings.detail: POMs get a code (A, B, C... or numeric 001, 002) in a logical measuring order; each has a how-to-measure description with method type: straight, curve, half circumference, full circumference, flat vs extended; standard abbreviations HPS, CB, CF, AH, SS. Chart columns: code, POM name, how-to-measure, tolerance (+/-), base size value, then each graded size, grade increment. Base size is the sample size (M for S/M/L). Measure in cm to 0.1 cm (or 0.5 cm steps for factory charts). Generic apparel tolerances: +/-1.0 cm most points, +/-0.5 cm collar/cuff/small trims, +/-1.5 cm body length. Headwear: +/-0.5 cm crown height, brim width/length, sweatband depth; +/-1.0 cm head circumference (adjustable), +/-0.5 cm finished circumference for fitted; check finished internal circumference after pressing because steaming can shift the opening 2-4 mm. Lot rejected if >20% of sampled pieces are out of tolerance.

findings.topic: Bucket hat size set and POM values (S/M/L)
findings.detail: EN 13402 head-girth bands: S 54-56, M 56-58, L 58-60 cm; OEM cap makers use S 55-56, M 57-58, L 59-60 cm. Recommended for prototype (finished inside circumference, measured at sweat line, full circumference): S 56.0, M 58.0, L 60.0 cm (+/-1.0) i.e. 2 cm grade; pattern adds 1-1.5 cm wearing ease. Crown/side-band height (side seam, tip seam to brim seam): 8.5-9.5 cm (+/-0.5), e.g. S 8.5 / M 9.0 / L 9.5 or hold 9.0-9.5 constant (Solbari holds 9.5 cm across sizes). Crown tip: diameter ~ (circ-4)/pi -> S 16.5 / M 17.2 / L 17.8 cm (+/-0.5). Brim width (band seam to edge, straight): 6.0 cm S/M, 6.5-7.0 cm L (+/-0.5); Solbari uses 6 cm S/M, 7 cm L/XL. Brim edge circumference derived. Total hat height (tip to brim edge) ~15-16 cm. Optional POMs: topstitch distance from seam 2-3 mm, eyelet dia (none here), label position from CB seam.

findings.topic: Construction section conventions (ISO 4915 / ISO 4916 / SPI / SA / topstitch / pressing)
findings.detail: Write each operation as: op no., operation name, seam class ISO 4916 (e.g. 1.01.01 superimposed plain seam; 2.02 lapped; 6.02 edge-neatening; 8.x for bindings), stitch type ISO 4915 (301 lockstitch, 401 two-thread chain, 504 three-thread overedge, 516 safety), SPI, seam allowance mm, thread Tex + needle Nm, machine type, pressing. Woven twill guidance: seaming 10-12 SPI (chino/dress pants), 8-10 SPI for heavier twill bottoms, topstitching 7-8 SPI; cap crown topstitch single needle 7-8 SPI 2 mm off seam; cap SA 6 mm, bucket hat SA 10 mm (DIY/industry patterns). Recommended bucket hat op list: (1) join 2 side-band pieces CB/CF, 301, 10-12 SPI, SA 10 mm, press open, topstitch each side 2 mm optional; (2) set crown tip to band, 301, SA 10 mm, notch, press SA down, topstitch band 3 mm below seam; (3) join brim halves, press open; (4) repeat 1-3 for reverse shell; (5) attach brim to each shell; (6) place shells right-sides-together at brim edge, 301 SA 10 mm, leave 6-8 cm gap, turn, press edge, close gap inside edge topstitch; (7) single-row brim edge topstitch 301, 8 SPI, 5 mm from edge, Tex 40; (8) tack shells together at band/brim seam (stitch-in-ditch) so hat reverses cleanly; (9) final press/steam, thread trim, inspection.

Colorway page lists each colorway with a code (CW1, CW2), name, a flat tinted per colorway, and a matrix of BOM components x colorway giving color name + Pantone TCX + hex + lab-dip status for each; start matching from the hardest-to-match item; reference systems: Pantone TCX (cotton), TPG, RGB/CMYK for artwork. Canonical case: CW1 'Khaki/Black' outer Khaki PANTONE 16-0726 TCX (#A39264), reverse Jet Black PANTONE 19-0303 TCX (#2D2C2F); CW2 'Black/Khaki' the inverse. Thread tonal to each shell: khaki side thread matched to 16-0726, black side to 19-0303 (for a single-row brim topstitch specify which side the needle thread faces and that bobbin is matched to the opposite shell). Labels: black ground/khaki text on both.

Label page: each label type with artwork ref, size mm, material (woven damask, printed satin, heat transfer), fold type (end-fold, centre-fold, loop), placement measured from a reference seam, sew method (301 4-side or 2-side). Care text/symbols per ISO 3758 (GINETEX symbols): 100% cotton twill hat = wash 30 C, no bleach, do not tumble dry, iron low, do not dry clean (or as tested). Packing: fold/flat method, polybag size/thickness, warning text, sticker with style/colour/size/barcode, hangtag placement, inner pack qty, assortment ratio (e.g. S:M:L = 1:2:1 or solid size cartons), master carton dims and gross weight cap, shipping marks. QC: ISO 2859-1 single sampling, General Inspection Level II, AQL 2.5 major / 4.0 minor (0 critical); for 1,201-3,200 pcs sample 125, for 3,201-10,000 sample 200; the widely quoted example is sample 315 accept 14 / reject 15 at AQL 2.5. Include measurement audit (min 10 pcs/size), defect classification list, and tests: fabric gsm, shrinkage (ISO 6330), colorfastness to washing (ISO 105-C06) and rubbing (ISO 105-X12), seam strength.

Proto (first sample, one size, checks design/feasibility) -> Fit sample (against spec, on form/model; often 2-3 rounds) -> Size set (graded run to verify grade rules) -> Salesman/photo samples (optional) -> PP / pre-production sample (bulk fabric & trims, on production line; buyer 'seals' it = gold seal / red tag) -> TOP (top of production, pulled from first bulk output and compared to PP) -> shipment sample. Tech pack should carry a sample log: stage, date sent/received, size, measured vs spec deviations, comments, approval status, approver. For a first-run small brand: proto + 1 fit + PP is a realistic minimum.

Goods sold in Egypt must carry non-erasable Arabic labels with country of origin, manufacturer's name and product description; labels may not be affixed after import (labels must be sewn in at the factory). Mandatory Egyptian Standard ES 7266 series 'Safety and health criteria and labelling for textile products' (EOS): Part 3 apparel and home textile (ES 7266-3/2023, obligatory, 37 pp, references EU 1007/2011 fibre names, REACH Annex XVII, EU 2014/350 Ecolabel), Part 4 garments (ES 7266-4:2011). Label elements per ES 7266-3: name/trademark, full fibre composition with percentages, care instructions (wash/bleach/iron), country of origin, manufacturer/importer name and address, net weight where applicable, warnings; restricted-chemical limits (banned azo dyes, formaldehyde per ISO 14184-1, nickel/cadmium, TRIS flame retardants). Care symbols per ES 1405/2014 which adopts ISO 3758:2012. Export goods entering Egypt from foreign factories additionally need GOEIC factory registration (Decree 43/2016, 44/2019) and Decree 477/2018 (ES 7322) for some textile/leather items. Practical rule for the tech pack: main label may be brand-only; care/content label must be bilingual Arabic/English with fibre % (e.g. 100% قطن / 100% cotton), care symbols + Arabic text, 'صنع في مصر / Made in Egypt', manufacturer name; put a size label with cm (e.g. M 58 سم).

EU: Regulation (EU) 1007/2011 fibre names and % in descending order in the language of the member state, durable label; care labelling voluntary but ISO 3758 symbols universal; (GPSR 2023/988 now requires manufacturer/importer name + address + product ID on product/packaging). UK: same as EU via Textile Products (Labelling and Fibre Composition) Regulations 2012. USA: Textile Fiber Products Identification Act - fibre content, country of origin on front of label, manufacturer name or RN; Care Labeling Rule 16 CFR 423 permanent care label; origin 'Made in Egypt' in English. GCC/Saudi (SASO/GSO): fibre content, care instructions and country of origin in Arabic (or Arabic+English); GSO 1956:2009 restricted substances. Practical: design a single 3-panel care label (Arabic / English + symbols / origin & RN placeholder) to cover Egypt, GCC, EU and US.

Fashion-incubator.com returned 403 to fetch; from search snippets and prior knowledge: Fasanella distinguishes a 'spec sheet' (measurement chart + sketch) from a full 'tech pack', warns that oversized templated tech packs overwhelm small contractors, and stresses that the pattern + approved sample are the true production authority, with the tech pack recording the sample's measured specs and grade. Her practical advice for small brands: fewer, correct POMs with realistic tolerances beat long lists; give the factory the sewing sequence and finished seam allowances. Treat as medium confidence.

findings.topic: MUST vs NICE for the prototype generator
findings.detail: MUST: header (style no., name, season, date, version, base size, size range, colorways, designer, status); product description & intended use; flats front/back/side + inside-out for reversible with lettered callouts; BOM (item, placement, description, composition, gsm, width, finish, supplier/ref placeholder, color ref TCX+hex, consumption/qty per unit, UoM, size-dependent flag); POM chart with code, how-to-measure, tolerance cm, S/M/L values, grade; construction ops with ISO 4915 stitch, ISO 4916 seam, SPI, SA mm, thread Tex, needle, pressing; topstitch spec; colorway matrix; label list with mandatory Arabic/English content and placement; basic packing (polybag, pcs/carton, carton marks); QC (AQL 2.5/4.0, key tests). NICE: cost sheet/target FOB, grading formulas per POM, detailed carton dimensions/board grade, embroidery/graphics page, sample-stage log with approver fields, fabric test standards list, fit comments history, marker/consumption yield, alternative suppliers, lab-dip approval tracking.

findings.source: synthesis; column conventions from Sewport, Techpacker, Apparel Entrepreneurship, Specter OS

recommendations: Implement the tech pack as the schema above and render it in the canonical order: header -> product description -> flats -> BOM -> POM chart -> construction -> colorways -> labels/packaging -> QC/compliance -> samples/revisions; keep costing and sample log as optional collapsed sections in the prototype.

Hard-code the headwear POM library for bucket hats (A inside circumference full-circ, B crown/side-band height, C crown tip diameter, D brim width, E total height, F brim edge circumference, G topstitch offset) with defaults S/M/L = 56/58/60 cm circumference (+/-1.0), 9.0-9.5 cm crown height (+/-0.5), 17.2 cm tip diameter base (+/-0.5), 6.0/6.0/6.5 cm brim (+/-0.5), and let the LLM adjust from the sketch/description rather than invent codes.

Encode a construction template per product type: for the bucket hat, 301 lockstitch, 10-12 SPI seaming, 8 SPI single-row brim edge topstitch 5 mm from edge, 10 mm SA, Tex 27-30 seaming / Tex 40 topstitch, needle Nm 80-90, tonal thread per shell, and an explicit reversible-assembly sequence (two complete shells, join at brim edge, turn, close, stitch-in-ditch tack).

Always emit color references as Pantone TCX + hex (Khaki 16-0726 TCX #A39264, Jet Black 19-0303 TCX #2D2C2F) and a BOM-by-colorway matrix so the factory can cut CW1 and CW2 from the same two fabric lots.

Generate a bilingual Arabic/English care-content label block by default for Egyptian brands: fibre % in Arabic and English, ISO 3758 symbols with Arabic care text (ES 1405/2014), 'صنع في مصر / Made in Egypt', manufacturer name and address, size in cm; flag that ES 7266-3/2023 is obligatory and that labels must be sewn in at the factory (no post-hoc stickers).

Include a compact QC block: ISO 2859-1 GII, AQL 2.5 major / 4.0 minor, measurement audit of 10 pcs per size, tests for gsm +/-5%, shrinkage <=3%, colorfastness to wash/rub; plus a proto -> fit -> PP -> TOP sample checklist with approver fields.

Mark all factory-dependent values (supplier refs, lab-dip numbers, exact consumption, carton dims) as 'TBC by factory' placeholders instead of hallucinated numbers, and show a confidence/assumption note per section so the user can review before sending to a masdrmena supplier.

Validate the generated POM chart programmatically: sizes must increase monotonically by the grade rule, tolerances present in cm, tip diameter consistent with circumference, and every POM code must appear as a callout on a sketch.
open_questions: Target markets for the first run: Egypt only, or also GCC/EU/US export? This decides whether the label block needs RN/EN/UK fields beyond Arabic+English.
Does the brand want a brand/main woven label on the reversible hat, and if so on which side (or a double-sided label in the brim seam)?
Should the size run be labelled S/M/L only, or S/M/L with cm (56/58/60) per EN 13402 practice?
Is the 280 gsm twill to be pre-shrunk/sanforized or will the factory pre-wash? This changes the pattern allowance and the shrinkage test requirement.
Preferred units for the factory: cm only, or cm with inches for export buyers?
Will the generator need cost-sheet output (fabric price, CMT, target FOB) in v1, or is it out of scope for the prototype?
Do you want the prototype to output the tech pack as JSON only, or also a rendered PDF/HTML page for the factory?

v2:e097dcc2869e91267420efc6cf0d5b9d0295c.summary: Recommended path: one EC2 t4g.small (2 vCPU/2 GiB Graviton, Ubuntu 24.04 arm64) in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), bootstrapped entirely by cloud-init user-data, fronted by Caddy for automatic Let's Encrypt/ZeroSSL TLS on masdr-proto.thegentek.com, with an Elastic IP, an instance profile (no long-lived keys on the box) for S3 + SSM, SSM Session Manager instead of SSH, SQLite on the root gp3 volume for metadata and S3 for uploads/generated packs, all in Terraform 1.15 with the S3 backend (native lockfile, no DynamoDB). It is the only option that (a) needs no container image (WSL2 has no docker), (b) has no 29s/30s gateway or 6 MB payload ceilings for 10 MB uploads and 60-120 s LLM calls, (c) needs only one manual DNS record at GoDaddy (A record masdr-proto -> EIP), and (d) works identically in eu-north-1 if you stay there. Frankfurt is chosen over Stockholm for ~18 ms better RTT from Cairo (68 ms vs 86 ms measured) and much broader service availability (App Runner, Bedrock EU inference); Stockholm is ~10% cheaper on compute. All-in cost is roughly $20/month in Frankfurt ($18 in Stockholm). Lambda+Function URL (RESPONSE_STREAM, 15 min timeout, 200 MB streamed response) behind CloudFront+ACM is the credible serverless runner-up at ~$1-5/month but adds CloudFront/ACM(us-east-1)/OAC plumbing, presigned-S3 uploads (6 MB sync request cap), and keepalive streaming to survive CloudFront's 30 s (max 120 s) per-packet origin timeout. Fargate needs CodeBuild for image builds plus an ALB (~$40/month total); Amplify Hosting SSR is ruled out by its 30 s compute timeout and 5.72 MB response cap; Lightsail ($12/month flat, available in both regions) is a fine budget fallback but cannot attach IAM roles, so S3 access would need static keys on the box.

findings.detail: App Runner is not available in eu-north-1 (Stockholm); it is available in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) since 2023-03-01, plus London/Paris/Mumbai since 2023-11-08. If you want a managed source-to-URL service it exists only if you move to Frankfurt; note its request timeout is 120 s max, marginal for 60-120 s generations.

findings.topic: Latency from Cairo to candidate regions (WonderNetwork, measured 2026-09-02)
findings.detail: Cairo->Frankfurt 67.8 ms, Cairo->Dublin 70.9 ms, Cairo->Stockholm 85.6 ms, Cairo->Milan 50.0 ms, Cairo->Tel Aviv 82.2 ms, Cairo->Manama (Bahrain) 109.7 ms, Cairo->Dubai 351 ms (routing anomaly). Frankfurt beats Stockholm by ~18 ms; Milan (eu-south-1) is closest but is an opt-in region with fewer services. Region RTT is negligible versus 30-120 s LLM latency; pick on service availability.

findings.topic: EC2 t4g.small on-demand price by region
findings.detail: t4g.small (2 vCPU Graviton2, 2 GiB, up to 5 Gbps): eu-central-1 $0.0192/h ($14.02/mo at 730 h), eu-north-1 $0.0172/h ($12.56/mo), eu-west-1 $0.0184/h, il-central-1 $0.0193/h. Add public IPv4 $0.005/h ($3.65/mo, charged since 2024-02-01 for every public IPv4 incl. EIP) and ~20 GB gp3 root (~$1.9/mo Frankfurt). Total EC2 path ~ $20/mo Frankfurt, ~ $18/mo Stockholm.

findings.topic: Lambda hard limits relevant to this app
findings.detail: Sync invocation payload 6 MB request / 6 MB response (BUFFERED); streamed response up to 200 MB (RESPONSE_STREAM, first 6 MB uncapped then 2 MB/s); function timeout 900 s; /tmp 512 MB-10 GB; zip 50 MB / 250 MB unzipped; memory 128 MB-10,240 MB (1 vCPU at 1,769 MB). Consequence: a 10 MB image upload cannot go through a Function URL body; use a presigned S3 PUT (browser -> S3) and pass the key to the function.

findings.topic: Lambda Function URL: streaming, timeout, custom domain
findings.detail: Function URLs use https://<id>.lambda-url.<region>.on.aws, are only public-internet, support CORS, auth NONE or AWS_IAM, and InvokeMode BUFFERED (6 MB) or RESPONSE_STREAM (200 MB, InvokeWithResponseStream). They do NOT support custom domain names; AWS docs point to API Gateway for custom domains, or you put CloudFront in front (CloudFront OAC for Lambda URL origins, GA 2024-04, requires AuthType AWS_IAM + lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl permission). Terraform: aws_lambda_function_url { authorization_type = "AWS_IAM" invoke_mode = "RESPONSE_STREAM" }.

Origin response (read) timeout: default 30 s, adjustable 1-120 s (quota increase beyond). It is a per-packet idle timeout, so a RESPONSE_STREAM Lambda that emits SSE/heartbeat bytes at least every ~25 s survives a 120 s generation; a silent buffered call does not. Optional 'response completion timeout' caps total; if unset there is no max. Request body limit 64 GB (not a constraint). ACM cert for a CloudFront alias must be issued in us-east-1.

findings.topic: API Gateway timeouts and payload caps
findings.detail: HTTP API: max integration timeout 30 s (not increasable), payload 10 MB. REST API: 29 s default; since 2024-06-04 you can raise it above 29 s for Regional and private REST APIs via Service Quotas (up to ~300 s), possibly at the cost of a lower account throttle quota; payload still 10 MB. API Gateway now also supports Lambda proxy response streaming (InvokeWithResponseStream, special output format with 8-null-byte delimiter). Verdict: API GW adds cost/complexity over a Function URL for no benefit here.

findings.topic: Lambda Web Adapter (run Express/FastAPI/Next unchanged on Lambda, zip packaging, no docker)
findings.detail: Attach layer arn:aws:lambda:<region>:753240598075:layer:LambdaAdapterLayerArm64:28 (or LambdaAdapterLayerX86:28), set AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER=/opt/bootstrap, handler = run.sh that starts your server on AWS_LWA_PORT (default 8080), AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE=response_stream, readiness check path/port. Docker alternative: COPY --from=public.ecr.aws/awsguru/aws-lambda-adapter:1.0.1 /lambda-adapter /opt/extensions/lambda-adapter. FastAPI + Bedrock streaming example exists in repo.

$0.20 per 1M requests; $0.0000166667 per GB-s (x86; arm64 ~20% less); free tier 1M requests + 400,000 GB-s/month. 1,000 generations x 90 s x 1 GB = 90,000 GB-s -> within free tier; beyond it ~$1.50 per 1,000 generations. Realistic Lambda+CloudFront+S3 prototype: $1-5/month.

Next.js SSR compute has a 30 s request timeout (long-standing open issue #3223/#3475), max response 5.72 MB (504 on exceed), build output 220 MB, Node 20+ required. A 60-120 s generation route cannot run there without offloading to another backend, which defeats the point.

findings.topic: ECS Fargate path: building an image without a local docker daemon
findings.detail: Use CodeBuild with an S3 zip as source (uploadable with the existing S3-only user), privileged mode on, arm1.small ($0.005/min, 100 free min/month on general1.small/arm1.small), buildspec: aws ecr get-login-password | docker login; docker build --platform linux/arm64; docker push. Nixpacks/pack need a docker daemon (not usable in this WSL2); ko is Go-only; GitHub Actions is the other daemon-free route. Fargate itself: ~$0.04048/vCPU-h + $0.004445/GB-h us-east-1, EU 10-30% higher, ARM 20% cheaper; 0.5 vCPU/1 GB ARM in Frankfurt ~ $15-17/mo, plus an ALB (~EUR 0.0266/h base in Frankfurt, ~$20-25/mo) for ACM TLS -> ~$40/mo and ~4x the IAM/Terraform surface of the EC2 path.

Available in both eu-north-1 and eu-central-1. $12/mo bundle = 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 60 GB SSD, 3 TB transfer, static IP included (free while attached; $0.005/h if idle); $7 = 1 GB RAM. Drawback: no IAM instance profile, so the app needs static access keys (or a Lightsail bucket) to reach S3, and SSM Session Manager is not native; Terraform aws_lightsail_instance supports user_data. Load balancer $18/mo (not needed with Caddy).

findings.topic: Caddy automatic HTTPS behaviour (recommended TLS approach)
findings.detail: Caddy 2 (apt via dl.cloudsmith.io caddy/stable repo, runs as systemd unit 'caddy') obtains certs from Let's Encrypt and automatically fails over to ZeroSSL, retries with exponential backoff up to 30 days, renews in the background, redirects HTTP->HTTPS, and stores certs under /var/lib/caddy. Requirements: A/AAAA record pointing at the box, ports 80 and 443 open, persistent data dir. Let's Encrypt duplicate-cert limit is 5 per exact name set per 7 days, so avoid repeatedly destroying/recreating the instance in one week (ZeroSSL fallback usually rescues you anyway). No ACM, ALB, or CloudFront needed; reverse_proxy has no response timeout by default, so 120 s LLM calls pass through; set request_body max_size 20MB.

findings.topic: ACM DNS validation with GoDaddy DNS (only if you choose ALB/CloudFront)
findings.detail: ACM emits one CNAME per name: _<32hex>.masdr-proto.thegentek.com -> _<32hex>.acm-validations.aws. Enter only the '_<hex>.masdr-proto' part in GoDaddy's Name field (it appends the zone). Validation typically <30 min, times out after 72 h; the CNAME must stay in place for auto-renewal and is reusable across regions (CloudFront needs the cert in us-east-1). Works with any third-party DNS.

findings.topic: GoDaddy DNS API access and record call
findings.detail: GoDaddy's 2024 restriction (10+ domains) was lifted in April 2026: DNS/Domain Management API needs just 1 domain in the account; keys from developer.godaddy.com/keys (separate OTE/prod); 60 req/min, 20k/month. Replace-record call: PUT https://api.godaddy.com/v1/domains/thegentek.com/records/A/masdr-proto with header 'Authorization: sso-key KEY:SECRET' and body [{"data":"<EIP>","ttl":600}] (min TTL 600). Terraform provider veksh/godaddy-dns (resource godaddy-dns_record) works but is unmaintained. Manual entry in the GoDaddy DNS UI is equally fine for one record.

findings.topic: Exact DNS record to create at GoDaddy (recommended path)
findings.detail: Type A, Name 'masdr-proto', Value = the Elastic IP output by Terraform, TTL 600. Do not CNAME to the ec2-*.compute.amazonaws.com name (changes on stop/start) and do not add AAAA unless you also assign an IPv6 address to the instance (Caddy would try to validate over it). If you instead pick Lambda+CloudFront: Type CNAME, Name 'masdr-proto', Value d<hash>.cloudfront.net, plus the ACM validation CNAME. ALB: CNAME to <name>.eu-central-1.elb.amazonaws.com plus ACM CNAME. The apex 216.198.79.193 (Vercel) is untouched.

findings.topic: EC2 user-data facts for the bootstrap
findings.detail: User data runs as root on first boot only (cloud-init), 16 KB raw limit, output in /var/log/cloud-init-output.log, script copied to /var/lib/cloud/instances/<id>/. Terraform aws_instance user_data (or user_data_base64) handles encoding. Use '#cloud-config' with packages/write_files/runcmd, and keep the app payload out of user-data (pull a release zip from S3 instead) to stay under 16 KB. Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 AMI via SSM public parameter /aws/service/canonical/ubuntu/server/24.04/stable/current/arm64/hvm/ebs-gp3/ami-id (data aws_ssm_parameter in Terraform; needs ssm:GetParameter).

findings.topic: SSM Session Manager instead of SSH
findings.detail: Needs SSM Agent >= 2.3.68.0 (preinstalled as a snap on Canonical Ubuntu AMIs and on AL2023), an instance profile with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, outbound 443 to ssm/ssmmessages/ec2messages.<region>.amazonaws.com, and the session-manager-plugin installed locally on WSL2 for 'aws ssm start-session'. Lets you close port 22 entirely; 'aws ssm send-command --document-name AWS-RunShellScript' is the deploy hook.

findings.topic: Minimum IAM for the recommended EC2+Terraform path (new IAM user or role; the current S3-only user cannot create it)
findings.detail: Deployer policy, region-scoped to eu-central-1 where possible: ec2:Describe* (Instances, Images, Vpcs, Subnets, SecurityGroups, Addresses, InstanceAttribute, InstanceTypes, Tags, Volumes, NetworkInterfaces, InstanceCreditSpecifications), ec2:RunInstances, TerminateInstances, StopInstances, StartInstances, ModifyInstanceAttribute, CreateTags, DeleteTags, CreateSecurityGroup, DeleteSecurityGroup, AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress/Egress, RevokeSecurityGroupIngress/Egress, AllocateAddress, AssociateAddress, DisassociateAddress, ReleaseAddress; iam:CreateRole, DeleteRole, GetRole, TagRole, AttachRolePolicy, DetachRolePolicy, PutRolePolicy, DeleteRolePolicy, GetRolePolicy, ListRolePolicies, ListAttachedRolePolicies, ListInstanceProfilesForRole, CreateInstanceProfile, DeleteInstanceProfile, GetInstanceProfile, AddRoleToInstanceProfile, RemoveRoleFromInstanceProfile, iam:PassRole (Resource = the one instance role ARN); ssm:GetParameter(s) on arn:aws:ssm:eu-central-1::parameter/aws/service/canonical/* and arn:aws:ssm:eu-central-1:<acct>:parameter/masdr-proto/*, ssm:PutParameter/DeleteParameter on /masdr-proto/*, ssm:StartSession, TerminateSession, SendCommand, GetCommandInvocation, DescribeInstanceInformation, ListCommandInvocations; s3:CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, GetBucket*, PutBucketPolicy, PutBucketPublicAccessBlock, PutBucketVersioning, PutBucketCors, PutLifecycleConfiguration, PutEncryptionConfiguration, ListBucket, GetObject, PutObject, DeleteObject on the app bucket and the tfstate bucket. Instance role: AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore + s3:GetObject/PutObject/ListBucket on the app bucket + ssm:GetParameter on /masdr-proto/* (+ kms:Decrypt on alias/aws/ssm for SecureString) + bedrock:InvokeModel/InvokeModelWithResponseStream if Bedrock is the LLM.

findings.topic: Minimum IAM for the alternative paths
findings.detail: Lambda+CloudFront: lambda:CreateFunction, UpdateFunctionCode, UpdateFunctionConfiguration, GetFunction, GetFunctionConfiguration, DeleteFunction, ListVersionsByFunction, PublishVersion, CreateAlias/UpdateAlias, Create/Update/Get/DeleteFunctionUrlConfig, AddPermission, RemovePermission, GetPolicy, PutFunctionConcurrency, TagResource, GetLayerVersion (on arn:aws:lambda:*:753240598075:layer:*); iam role CRUD + PassRole for the execution role (AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole + s3/dynamodb); logs:CreateLogGroup, PutRetentionPolicy, DescribeLogGroups, DeleteLogGroup; cloudfront:CreateDistribution, UpdateDistribution, GetDistribution, GetDistributionConfig, DeleteDistribution, TagResource, ListTagsForResource, CreateOriginAccessControl, GetOriginAccessControl, DeleteOriginAccessControl, GetCachePolicy, GetOriginRequestPolicy, CreateInvalidation; acm (us-east-1): RequestCertificate, DescribeCertificate, DeleteCertificate, AddTagsToCertificate, ListTagsForCertificate; s3 bucket + CORS as above; optional dynamodb:CreateTable/DescribeTable/UpdateTable/DeleteTable/TagResource/ListTagsOfResource + runtime PutItem/GetItem/Query/UpdateItem. Fargate: all of the above bucket/logs perms plus ecr:CreateRepository/Describe*/GetAuthorizationToken/Batch*/PutImage/InitiateLayerUpload/UploadLayerPart/CompleteLayerUpload/DeleteRepository, codebuild:CreateProject/UpdateProject/DeleteProject/BatchGetProjects/StartBuild/BatchGetBuilds, ecs:CreateCluster/DeleteCluster/Describe*/RegisterTaskDefinition/DeregisterTaskDefinition/CreateService/UpdateService/DeleteService/TagResource, elasticloadbalancing:* (CreateLoadBalancer, CreateTargetGroup, CreateListener, Modify*, Describe*, Delete*, AddTags), acm in-region, ec2 VPC/SG Describe+CreateSecurityGroup etc., iam roles for CodeBuild service role (AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryPowerUser + logs), ecsTaskExecutionRole (AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy) and task role. Lightsail: lightsail:CreateInstances, GetInstance(s), DeleteInstance, AllocateStaticIp, AttachStaticIp, ReleaseStaticIp, GetStaticIp(s), PutInstancePublicPorts, OpenInstancePublicPorts, GetInstanceAccessDetails, CreateKeyPair, TagResource, GetRegions, GetBlueprints, GetBundles (+ an IAM user access key for S3 from inside the instance). Amplify: amplify:* on the app + iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole + a GitHub connection.

Terraform >= 1.10 supports S3 backend native locking (use_lockfile = true), so with Terraform 1.15 the existing S3-only credentials are enough for state; no dynamodb permissions required. Key suggestion: bucket=<existing>, key=masdr-proto/terraform.tfstate, region=eu-central-1, encrypt=true.

findings.topic: Bedrock in EU regions (only if Bedrock is the LLM)
findings.detail: Anthropic Claude models are offered in Europe via EU cross-region inference profiles that include Frankfurt, Ireland, Paris and Stockholm (Claude 3.7 Sonnet announced 2025-04; newer models follow the same EU profile pattern). Frankfurt lists more Bedrock models/deployment types than Stockholm. If you call the Anthropic API directly, region is irrelevant to the LLM.

recommendations: Choose Path A: EC2 t4g.small + Caddy + cloud-init, Terraform-managed, in eu-central-1. Rationale: no container build, no gateway timeouts, direct 10 MB multipart uploads through Caddy, SQLite on disk, instance-profile credentials, one A record at GoDaddy, ~$20/month. Keep the same Terraform if you later decide to stay in eu-north-1 (only price and RTT change).

Runbook step 0 (account admin, one-off): create IAM user 'masdr-proto-deployer' (or a role assumed via 'aws sts assume-role') with the EC2-path policy listed in findings; 'aws configure --profile masdr' on WSL2; export AWS_REGION=eu-central-1; install session-manager-plugin .deb (sudo dpkg -i session-manager-plugin.deb).

Step 1 (Terraform backend): terraform { backend "s3" { bucket = "<existing-bucket>" key = "masdr-proto/terraform.tfstate" region = "eu-central-1" encrypt = true use_lockfile = true } }. Provider aws region eu-central-1, default_tags Project=masdr-proto.

Step 2 (Terraform resources): data aws_ssm_parameter ubuntu { name = "/aws/service/canonical/ubuntu/server/24.04/stable/current/arm64/hvm/ebs-gp3/ami-id" }; aws_default_vpc + default subnet; aws_security_group ingress 80 and 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0, no 22, egress all; aws_iam_role + aws_iam_instance_profile with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and an inline policy for s3:GetObject/PutObject/ListBucket on the app bucket and ssm:GetParameter on arn:aws:ssm:eu-central-1:<acct>:parameter/masdr-proto/*; aws_s3_bucket 'masdr-proto-data-<acct>' with public access block, SSE-S3, lifecycle expiring uploads/ after 30 days; aws_ssm_parameter '/masdr-proto/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' type SecureString (pass via TF_VAR, or write with 'aws ssm put-parameter' outside Terraform to keep it out of state); aws_instance t4g.small, ami = data.aws_ssm_parameter.ubuntu.value, root_block_device gp3 20 GB, metadata_options http_tokens = "required", user_data = templatefile("cloud-init.yaml", { domain, bucket, region }); aws_eip + aws_eip_association; output eip.

Step 3 (cloud-init.yaml, < 16 KB): #cloud-config; packages: unzip, curl, ca-certificates, debian-keyring, debian-archive-keyring, apt-transport-https, (nodejs via NodeSource 22.x in runcmd, or python3-venv); write_files: /etc/caddy/Caddyfile = 'masdr-proto.thegentek.com { encode gzip; request_body { max_size 20MB }; reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 }' (add 'basic_auth { user hash }' to gate the prototype); /etc/systemd/system/masdr.service (User=masdr, WorkingDirectory=/opt/masdr/current, EnvironmentFile=/etc/masdr/env, ExecStart=/usr/bin/node server.js, Restart=always, RestartSec=3); /usr/local/bin/masdr-deploy (aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/releases/latest.zip /tmp; unzip to /opt/masdr/releases/<ts>; npm ci --omit=dev; ln -sfn to /opt/masdr/current; systemctl restart masdr); runcmd: add Caddy cloudsmith repo (curl -1sLf https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg; curl -1sLf .../debian.deb.txt > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list; apt update; apt install -y caddy awscli), useradd masdr, write /etc/masdr/env from 'aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption' (chmod 600, PORT=8080, S3_BUCKET, AWS_REGION), /usr/local/bin/masdr-deploy, systemctl enable --now masdr caddy, enable unattended-upgrades.

Step 4 (first apply order to avoid burning Let's Encrypt attempts): terraform apply -target=aws_eip.app -> create the GoDaddy A record masdr-proto -> <EIP> TTL 600 (UI, or PUT https://api.godaddy.com/v1/domains/thegentek.com/records/A/masdr-proto with 'Authorization: sso-key KEY:SECRET' and body [{"data":"<EIP>","ttl":600}]) -> upload the first release zip to s3://<bucket>/releases/latest.zip (works with today's S3-only creds) -> terraform apply (full). Caddy retries automatically if DNS is still propagating.

Step 5 (verify): dig +short masdr-proto.thegentek.com; curl -I https://masdr-proto.thegentek.com; aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id> then 'journalctl -u caddy -u masdr -n 200' and 'tail /var/log/cloud-init-output.log'.

Step 6 (deploy loop, no docker, no SSH): zip -r release.zip . -x 'node_modules/*' '.git/*' && aws s3 cp release.zip s3://<bucket>/releases/latest.zip && aws ssm send-command --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --targets Key=tag:Name,Values=masdr-proto --parameters 'commands=["/usr/local/bin/masdr-deploy"]' ; poll with aws ssm get-command-invocation.

App-shape guidance for either path: make POST /generate return a job id immediately and stream progress over SSE (or poll GET /jobs/{id}), persisting the job row in SQLite (EC2) or DynamoDB/S3 JSON (Lambda), so a browser refresh or proxy hiccup during a 120 s generation does not lose the result; write the finished tech pack (JSON + rendered PDF/XLSX) to s3://<bucket>/packs/<job>/ and serve via presigned GET.

Robustness add-ons worth their cost: EBS daily snapshot via aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy (needs dlm:* + ec2:CreateSnapshot in the deployer policy), CloudWatch agent for disk/mem alarms, an aws_budgets_budget alert at $30, and IMDSv2-only. Do not run terraform destroy/apply of the instance more than a few times per week (Let's Encrypt duplicate-cert limit 5/week; ZeroSSL fallback exists).

If you later want zero-idle-cost: Path B = Lambda (arm64, 2048 MB, 300 s timeout) + Lambda Web Adapter layer (LambdaAdapterLayerArm64:28, AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE=response_stream) + Function URL (AWS_IAM, RESPONSE_STREAM) + CloudFront (OAC lambda origin, response timeout raised to 120 s, ACM cert in us-east-1, alias masdr-proto.thegentek.com -> CNAME d<hash>.cloudfront.net at GoDaddy) + presigned S3 PUT uploads (6 MB sync cap) + SSE heartbeats every <=25 s. Skip API Gateway entirely (30 s HTTP API hard cap; REST needs a quota exception).

Do not choose Amplify Hosting (30 s SSR timeout, 5.72 MB response cap) or Fargate for this prototype (CodeBuild image pipeline + ALB pushes cost to ~$40/month and IAM surface up 4x with no functional gain at one instance). Lightsail $12/month is acceptable only if the budget, not credential hygiene, is the binding constraint.
open_questions: Who in the AWS account can create the new IAM user/role (the current user has no iam:* rights) and do they prefer a long-lived user with access keys or an assumable role with MFA?

Is the LLM called via the Anthropic API directly or via Amazon Bedrock? (Bedrock changes the instance-role policy and makes eu-central-1 a stronger choice; direct API makes region irrelevant to the model.)
Node.js or Python for the app? (Decides NodeSource vs python3-venv in cloud-init and the systemd ExecStart; the Lambda Web Adapter fallback supports both.)
Do you have (or can you get) GoDaddy API keys for thegentek.com, or will the A record be added manually in the GoDaddy DNS UI? Who owns that GoDaddy account?

Should the prototype be gated (Caddy basic_auth or a shared link token) before Egyptian brand users see it, and is there any data-residency requirement for uploaded product photos that would rule out EU regions?
Expected concurrency for demos (a single t4g.small comfortably handles ~10 simultaneous I/O-bound generations; more needs t4g.medium or the Lambda path)?
Is a monthly ceiling of roughly $20-25 acceptable, or is the target closer to $0 idle (which would favour the Lambda path despite its extra plumbing)?
Do you want to keep eu-north-1 for account-default consistency (everything in the runbook works there; -$1.50/month, +18 ms RTT, no App Runner) or switch the prototype to eu-central-1 as recommended?

v2:4726761704c0f9ba8da2d4678a68b609a02a6.summary: A reversible cotton-twill bucket hat is built as two complete self-fabric shells (each = 1 top circle + 2 side-band panels + 2 half-annulus brim panels), joined right-sides-together around the brim outer edge, turned through a 6-8 cm gap, and locked with the brim topstitch; there is no separate lining, no sweatband, and normally no metal eyelets. Verified adult sizing for the S/M/L test case is head 54-56/56-58/58-60 cm with finished inside circumference 57/59/61 cm (1 cm ease, 2 cm grade), crown height at side 8.5/9.0/9.5 cm, top-circle diameter ~17.4/18.0/18.6 cm and a 6.5 cm brim (brim outer circumference ~98/100/102 cm). Fabric: 100% cotton 3/1 twill 20x16 / 128x60, 270-280 gsm (~8.3 oz/yd²), 147-150 cm wide, sanforized (residual shrinkage <=3%), ~0.20 m of each colour per hat at 150 cm width. Sewing is 301 lockstitch on DBx1 Nm 80-90 with Tex 27-30 (Tkt 120/100) core-spun poly for seaming and Tex 40 (Tkt 75/80) on Nm 90-100 for the single brim topstitch at 6 mm from the edge, 10-12 SPI (Coats spec: 12-14 st/3 cm); needle thread khaki / bobbin black so each face shows its own colour. With only one topstitch row at 2 x 280 gsm the brim is soft, so spec a 50-70 gsm woven fusible on one brim (cut on bias, trimmed out of the seam allowance) or accept a packable brim. No published headwear SAM exists; an operation-based estimate is ~11-13 sewing SAM (~15 min incl. finishing/packing). Key tech-pack insight: the two stated colourways are physically the same hat unless the brand label side or a detail differentiates them.

findings.topic: Pattern pieces and reversible construction principle
findings.detail: Each shell = 3 pattern pieces: (1) crown tip/top circle x1, (2) side crown/band x2 (seamed at left and right sides; some patterns cut it as 1 piece with a CB seam), (3) brim half-annulus x2 cut on fold/seamed at sides so brim seams align with band seams. A reversible hat is two full self-fabric shells (Fabric A khaki, Fabric B black) - no separate lining, no sweatband. Shells are joined only at the brim outer edge; the crowns float independently. Pattern blogs (AppleGreen, Peekaboo, Hello Sewing, Spoonflower) all use 1 cm (3/8 in) SA; Merchant & Mills industrial-style pattern also 1 cm SA included; Oliver+S uses 1/2 in SA trimmed to 1/4-1/8 in after sewing.

findings.topic: Turning opening and closing method (industrial vs hand)
findings.detail: Two documented methods. (A) Bag-out at brim: shells placed RS together, sew the brim outer edge at 1 cm leaving a 5-8 cm gap (blogs specify 1-2 in, 2 in, 3 in), trim/grade SA to ~5 mm, notch, turn through gap, press edge, then the brim topstitch closes the gap by catching the folded SA - no hand work; this is the machine method used by Peekaboo, Spoonflower, Hello Sewing, AppleGreen. (B) Oliver+S: join the two brims first, attach brim to shell A, then fold shell B's lower SA under and blind-stitch it by hand over the seam - not suitable for production. Recommendation for factory: method A with the gap centred at CB of the brim edge (6-8 cm), closed by the single 6 mm topstitch row; add an optional stitch-in-ditch or 2 mm edge-stitch along the brim/band seam to stop the two shells rotating relative to each other.

Industry charts converge on S 54-56 cm, M 56-58 cm, L 58-60 cm, XL 60-62 cm (bon-clic-bon-genre/Lock Hatters); mfgmerch: S 53.3-55.2, M 55.2-57.8, L 57.8-59.7; Sumkcaps bucket-hat chart: S 54-55, M 56-57, L 58-59, XL 60-61. Average adult female = 57 cm, male = 59 cm. Metric grade between sizes is 1 cm for fitted hats, 2 cm for S/M/L alpha sizing. Ease: add 1-1.5 cm to head measurement for the finished inside circumference (1 cm for 7 oz twill, 1.5 cm for rigid denim - Happyoff). Merchant & Mills finished circumferences M 57.5 / L 59.5 / XL 61.5 cm confirm ~+1.5 cm ease and 2 cm grade. Recommended spec for test case: S fits 55-56 -> finished 57.0; M 57-58 -> 59.0; L 59-60 -> 61.0 cm.

findings.topic: Crown height, top diameter, brim width by size and grade increments
findings.detail: Sumkcaps (manufacturer): crown (top) diameter S 16.5-17 / M 17.5-18 / L 18.5-19 / XL 19.5-20 cm; crown depth S 8.5-9 / M 9-9.5 / L 9.5-10 cm; brim S 5-5.5 / M 5.5-6 / L 6-6.5 / XL 6.5-7 cm. Solbari: brim 6.5 cm (S/M) and 7 cm (L/XL), crown depth at side 8.5 / 9 cm. MeasuringKnowHow: brim 5-7.6 cm, crown 5-10 cm typical. Nury: 9 cm crown, 7 cm brim, ~29 cm overall silhouette. Geometry: top-circle diameter = top circumference / pi; a 2 cm circumference grade = 0.64 cm diameter grade. Recommended spec (finished, cm): top diameter S 17.4 / M 18.0 / L 18.6 (grade 0.6); crown height at side S 8.5 / M 9.0 / L 9.5 (grade 0.5); brim width 6.5 all sizes (or 6.5/6.5/7.0); brim outer circumference = inside circ + 2*pi*6.5 = ~97.8 / 99.8 / 101.8; overall brim-edge diameter ~31.1 / 31.8 / 32.4; hat total height ~15.5-16.5.

Recommended POMs (measure flat, inside, at brim/band seam): A Inside circumference at brim seam +/-1.0 cm; B Crown height at side seam (brim seam to top seam) +/-0.5; C Top-circle diameter (seam to seam) +/-0.5; D Brim width (brim seam to edge, at 4 points: CF, CB, L, R) +/-0.3; E Brim outer circumference +/-1.5; F Total height (top to brim edge, hat standing) +/-0.5; G Topstitch distance from brim edge 6 mm +/-1 mm; H Side-seam alignment between shells <=5 mm offset; I Turning-gap closure position CB +/-2 cm. Basis: soft hats tolerate +/-0.5-1.0 cm circumference (Reference.com); no published bucket-hat tolerance table exists, so values are derived from hat-size grade (a 1.27 cm error = one fitted size) and general apparel practice.

280 gsm = 8.26 oz/yd2 (1 oz/yd2 = 33.9 gsm; Fashion-Incubator chart). Standard mill construction for 270-280 gsm 100% cotton twill: 3/1 twill, yarn 20s x 16s Ne, density 128 x 60 (ends x picks per inch), width 57/58 in (147 cm) - available at 58/60 in; 240 gsm version is same construction lighter finish. 3/1 has longer floats and softer hand but is slightly less stable than 2/1; unsanforized cotton can shrink 5-10%, sanforized targets <1% residual, common buyer tolerance for dimensional change (AATCC 135, 3 washes) is <=3% warp/weft. Pattern blogs and Happyoff recommend 7-9 oz (240-300 gsm) twill/canvas for bucket hats; Merchant & Mills suggests mid-weight canvas/8-13 oz denim. Spec line: 100% cotton, 3/1 twill (Z), 20x16 / 128x60, 280 gsm +/-5%, 147-150 cm cuttable, reactive dyed, sanforized, residual shrinkage <=3% x <=3%, colourfastness to rubbing dry >=4 / wet >=3 (AATCC 8) - critical because black is in permanent contact with khaki (MUJI warns of dark-colour transfer on its twill bucket hat). Relax fabric 24 h before cutting; run a shrinkage test per colour lot.

Home patterns quote 0.5 yd (45 cm) of outer + 0.5 yd lining at 36-45 in width, or 35 cm of 36 in fabric per shell (Hello Sewing); Merchant & Mills: 0.5 m self at 80 cm width (narrow brim) + 0.3 m lining. Computed for size M with 1 cm SA: top circle ~21.5x21.5 cm, 2 band panels ~32x11 cm, 2 brim halves ~35x17 cm -> ~0.23 m2 net per shell, 0.46 m2 net per hat. At 75-80% marker efficiency (multi-size marker on 150 cm) -> ~0.60 m2 gross = ~0.40 m of 150 cm fabric per hat total, i.e. ~0.20 m khaki + ~0.20 m black per hat (allow 0.22-0.25 m each incl. 5% cutting loss for first run). Net fabric weight ~130 g; finished hat ~135-150 g (listed product weights of 7-8 oz for twill bucket hats are shipping weights).

Coats cap application guide: panel assembly 301 lockstitch, Coats Epic (poly core-spun) Tex 24 / Tkt 120 or Astra spun poly Tex 27 / Tkt 120; embroidery Sylko Tex 27. Coats work-caps guide (heavier twill): Epic Tex 40 / Tkt 80, needle Nm 80-90, 12-14 stitches per 3 cm (= 10-12 SPI). Tex-to-ticket: Tkt = 3000/Tex (Tex 27->Tkt 110/120, Tex 30->Tkt 100, Tex 40->Tkt 75/80, Tex 60->Tkt 50). Needle: DBx1 (1738/16x257) is the plain single-needle lockstitch system Nm 65-110; DPx5 (135x5) is for zigzag/bartack/pattern sewers/twin-needle and automatic brim stitchers, Nm 70-140; R (round/sharp) point for twill; Nm 100-110 suggested for denim/twill workwear, Nm 80-90 adequate for 2-4 plies of 280 gsm. Recommendation: seaming Tex 27-30 core-spun poly (Tkt 120/100), DBx1 Nm 80-90 R; brim topstitch Tex 40 core-spun (Tkt 75/80), Nm 90-100, 10-11 SPI (spec 10-12); optional bold look Tex 60 / Tkt 50 on Nm 100-110. Reversible colour rule: needle thread matches the face up (khaki), bobbin thread matches the other face (black) - balance tension so neither shows through; specify both thread colours in the BOM.

Pattern sources: Oliver+S concentric rows 1/4 in (6 mm) apart; Spoonflower every 3/8 in (10 mm); Hello Sewing every 1/2 in (12.5 mm), 5-6 rows; Peekaboo edge-stitch + ~4 rows using presser-foot width. Commercial caps run 4-8 parallel rows on a machine with a spacing guide; programmable bucket-hat brim stitchers (JYL) sew concentric rows automatically. Test case = single row at 6 mm from brim edge: sew with an edge guide/compensating foot, 10-11 SPI, start/stop at CB side seam with 1 cm overlap (no backtack visible), this row also closes the turning gap. Note in tech pack that a single row gives a soft brim; offer 3 rows at 6/12/18 mm as an upgrade option.

findings.topic: Brim interfacing for reversible at 280 gsm
findings.detail: Two 280 gsm plies give a 560 gsm brim; AppleGreen (double-layer construction) and many reversible patterns use no interfacing and rely on multiple stitch rows. Oliver+S and Peekaboo interface only ONE shell's brim (Fabric B) for a reversible hat; interfacing must be trimmed out of the SA and should be lighter than the shell fabric (Elbe Textiles). Happyoff: woven fusible cut at 45 deg to grain gives the brim spring; firm fusible for brims, medium woven for crowns. Available woven fusibles: 40-80 gsm (shirt-collar 60-70 gsm; 80 gsm heavy). Recommendation for test case with single topstitch row: 50-70 gsm woven fusible (polyester or cotton) on the black shell's brim only, cut on bias, trimmed 1 cm inside the cut edge; fuse per supplier datasheet (typ. 140-160 C, 2.5-4 bar, 12-18 s on a flat press), wash-test for bubbling. If brand wants a packable/soft hat, omit interfacing and state 'unstructured brim' in the tech pack.

findings.topic: Sweatband, eyelets, and other non-reversible components
findings.detail: Non-reversible twill bucket hats carry a polyester inner sweatband (MUJI: body 100% cotton, inner band 100% polyester), 2 embroidered or metal eyelets per side (H&M, Patagonia) and multi-row brim stitching (OUYI, Unionwear). Reversible hats omit the sweatband (both faces are outer faces); eyelets are usually omitted because metal eyelets would have to pass through both shells and show a washer on one side. Options if ventilation is required: 2 embroidered eyelets (dia. ~8 mm) per side on each shell, done before assembly, in matching thread. Adjustable drawcord/hidden strap (MUJI) not applicable. Test case: no sweatband, no eyelets, no chin strap - state explicitly in tech pack so the factory does not add them.

findings.topic: Label placement on a reversible hat
findings.detail: Standard cap placement is the sweatband or crown lining (Super Label Store); neither exists on a reversible hat, and any label is visible when the other side is worn. Practical options used commercially: (1) small woven loop/flag label caught in the side seam of the designated 'inside' shell (black shell for colourway 1) ~2 cm above the brim seam - stitching is hidden in the seam; (2) folded woven label sewn flat at CB of the designated inner shell just above brim seam; (3) heat-transfer/printed care & content label inside the crown top of the designated inner shell (Uniqlo-style printed labels avoid a second sewn label). US FTC allows a temporary (hangtag) care label for fully reversible garments provided the label says 'Wash or dryclean, any normal method'; otherwise use a single loop label with brand on one face and fibre/care/size/origin on the reverse. Recommend: one woven loop label (brand + size) in left side seam of black shell + printed care/content on the back of that label or a heat-transfer inside black crown; hangtag carries reversibility story.

findings.topic: Sewing sequence (operation breakdown with machine and estimated SAM)
findings.detail: Cutting: relax fabric 24 h, spread, cut (straight knife), fuse brim B on flat press, bundle by size/colour. Sewing (SNLS = single-needle lockstitch 301, DBx1): for EACH shell - 1) join band side seams x2, 1 cm (SNLS, 0.5 min) [insert woven label in left seam of black shell, +0.3]; 2) press seams open (iron, 0.3); 3) join brim halves x2 (SNLS, 0.5); 4) press brim seams open (0.2); 5) set top circle to band, 4 notches, ease band to circle (SNLS, 1.2); 6) set brim to band matching side seams (SNLS, 1.0) = ~3.7 min per shell, 7.4 for two. Assembly: 7) place shells RS together, sew brim outer edge 1 cm leaving 7 cm gap at CB (SNLS, 1.2); 8) trim/grade SA to 5 mm and notch (manual, 0.5); 9) turn, roll edge, press brim flat (iron, 1.0); 10) topstitch brim 1 row at 6 mm closing gap (SNLS with edge guide or programmable brim stitcher, 1.0); 11) optional stitch-in-ditch at brim/band seam (SNLS, 0.8); 12) thread trim + inspect (0.8); 13) final steam/press on form (0.7); 14) hangtag, fold, polybag (0.7). Estimated total sewing SAM ~11-13 min, ~15 min including finishing/packing. No published headwear SAM exists; figures are estimates built with the standard SAM method (observed time x rating x (1+allowance)) and should be validated on the first bundle.
findings.source: https://www.onlineclothingstudy.com/2011/02/how-to-calculate-sam-of-garment.html ; https://ordnur.com/apparel/standard-allowed-minutes-sam/ ; https://www.jylsewing.com/hat-stitching-machine/bucket-hat-sewing-machine/ ; construction sequence from pattern sources above

findings.detail: Press band and brim seams open before assembly (Oliver+S trims to 6 mm after pressing); after turning, roll the brim seam exactly to the edge (no 'lip' of the other colour showing) and press flat before topstitching; press interfacing per datasheet, using stamp method not sliding (Happyoff); final light steam on a crown form - do not crease crown.
