Check no shine/glazing on black twill (use press cloth).

findings.topic: QC checks, AQL and common defects
findings.detail: Hat inspection uses ISO 2859-1 sampling; typical: critical 0 / major AQL 2.5 / minor AQL 4.0. Critical: sharp metal, mould/odour, missing legal label. Major: wrong fabric/colour, deformed crown, wrong size, poor/wavy brim, noticeable stain, missing brand label. Minor: loose thread, slight label shift, packing wrinkle. Reversible-specific checks: circumference at brim seam within +/-1 cm; brim width at 4 points +/-0.3 cm; topstitch 6 mm +/-1 mm and parallel; SPI 10-12; side seams of the two shells aligned (<=5 mm); no bobbin colour showing on either face; turning gap fully closed and no needle holes; shade consistency within lot (khaki lots are prone to shade variation); crocking test black->khaki; brim lies flat (no wave/pucker from mismatched ease or over-stiff fusible); no fusible bubbling after wash test; crown not twisted; top-circle seam without pleats. Measurement per ctstek/CNCAPS: inspectors measure head circumference with calibrated tools against approved sample.

Bucket hats are crushable and normally packed flat/folded: fold in half with brim folded to avoid creasing (buy4store) or flat-stacked; individual polybag with air hole and size sticker, 10-12 per inner bundle, 100-200 per export carton (5-ply, B+C flute); carton marks: style, colourway, size breakdown, qty, CoO; size/colour separation per carton and packing-list match (jointopcap, QC guides). Unstructured hats do not need crown protection blocks. For a first small run recommend flat pack, 1 pc/polybag, 50 pcs/carton.

findings.topic: Colourway definition for the test case
findings.detail: Colourway 1 'khaki outer / black reverse' and colourway 2 'black outer / khaki reverse' are physically the same garment (both shells present in every hat); they differ only in which side carries the brand label / is presented in packaging. Tech pack should either merge to one SKU with a 'default face' note or define the differentiator (label side, hangtag, thread colour). Suggested colour standards: Khaki PANTONE 16-0726 TCX (hex approx #C3B091, 'khaki'), Black PANTONE 19-0303 TCX Jet Black (#0A0A0A); thread: needle khaki-match, bobbin black-match (and vice versa for the black-face default); label ground to match black shell; lab-dip both colours on the 280 gsm twill.
findings.source: industry knowledge (Pantone TCX references); construction sources above

findings.detail: Uniqlo Unisex Reversible Bucket Hat: garment-washed cotton, solid one side / check other; Patagonia Bucket Hat (non-reversible): organic cotton canvas, flat top, unstructured crown, side eyelets, stitched brim; MUJI cotton twill bucket hat: one size 56.5-59 cm, poly inner band, hidden adjuster; H&M cotton twill bucket hat: embroidered eyelets, sweatband; Merchant & Mills bucket hat pattern: sizes M/L/XL = 57.5/59.5/61.5 cm, narrow brim 4.8 cm, wide brim 11.4 cm, 1 cm SA. Automatic bucket-hat brim stitchers (JYL) exist for concentric-row brims; one operator can run several units.

recommendations: Generator spec chart for the test case (finished cm, S/M/L): inside circumference at brim seam 57/59/61 (+/-1.0), crown height at side 8.5/9.0/9.5 (+/-0.5), top-circle diameter 17.4/18.0/18.6 (+/-0.5), brim width 6.5/6.5/6.5 (+/-0.3), brim outer circumference 97.8/99.8/101.8 (+/-1.5), total height 15.0/15.5/16.0 (+/-0.5), topstitch 0.6 from edge (+/-0.1). State 'fits head 55-56 / 57-58 / 59-60 cm' on the size label.

Construction block: two full 280 gsm twill shells (1 top, 2 band, 2 brim halves each), 1 cm SA, shells joined RS-together at brim outer edge leaving 6-8 cm gap at CB, SA graded to 5 mm and notched, turned, pressed, single 301 topstitch at 6 mm closing the gap; add stitch-in-ditch at brim/band seam as recommended default. No lining, no sweatband, no eyelets, no strap - say so explicitly.

BOM: 100% cotton 3/1 twill 20x16 128x60, 280 gsm, 147-150 cm, sanforized <=3%, khaki + black, ~0.22 m each per hat; woven fusible 50-70 gsm on black brim only (optional, bias-cut); thread Tex 27-30 core-spun poly for seaming (khaki + black), Tex 40 core-spun for topstitch (khaki needle / black bobbin); woven loop label; heat-transfer or printed care label; hangtag; polybag.

Sewing notes: 301 lockstitch, DBx1 Nm 80-90 R for seaming, Nm 90-100 for topstitch, 10-12 SPI; DPx5 only if the factory uses an automatic brim stitcher; balance tension so no bobbin colour shows on either face; match band and brim seams across both shells; ease band to top circle with 4 notches.

Quality: run shrinkage and crocking tests on each colour lot before cutting (black onto khaki is the main risk); use AQL 2.5 major / 4.0 minor with the reversible-specific checklist above; approve a size-M sealed sample of each face before bulk.
Flag the colourway issue to the client: 'khaki outer/black reverse' and 'black outer/khaki reverse' are the same hat; decide whether to ship one SKU or differentiate by label side/hangtag.
Mark SAM figures in the output as estimates (~11-13 sewing min, ~15 total) pending a first-bundle time study; there is no published headwear SAM.
open_questions: Is the brim intended to be soft/packable (no interfacing, single topstitch) or structured (add fusible on one brim and/or 3 rows at 6/12/18 mm)?
Are the two colourways meant to be one SKU (same physical hat) or two SKUs differentiated by brand-label side / hangtag / thread colour?
Which face carries the woven brand label and care/content label, and does the brand accept a printed/heat-transfer care label inside one crown (visible when reversed)?
Egyptian labelling requirements (Arabic care/content label, country of origin) for a domestic first run - and is export (EU/US care-label rules) planned?
Band construction preference: 2 side seams (aligns with 2-piece brim) or single CB seam?
Confirm size label convention: S/M/L alpha only, or also print the cm range (55-56 / 57-58 / 59-60)?

Fabric sourcing: is the 280 gsm twill already sourced (mill spec sheet with shrinkage/colourfastness available), or should the tech pack specify a target construction (20x16 / 128x60) for local Egyptian mills?
Is ventilation required (embroidered eyelets on each shell) or acceptable to omit?
Target order quantity and size ratio (affects marker efficiency and the consumption figure).

v2:ac341bce221c0fb55523bdf58df742944a371.summary: Factories consume a tech pack as a locked PDF (one section per page, sketch and its notes on the same page, numbered POMs tied to a diagram) plus an editable XLSX for the BOM and measurement chart; Excel-only packs drift between machines and are the format factories complain about. Egyptian/MENA makers (e.g. Kemora, Cairo, MOQ 50/colour; Thread Gate, MOQ 500) explicitly accept "photo, sketch, sample or tech pack", and Arabic-market tech-pack services deliver PDF/JPG/PNG with English section names transliterated or glossed in Arabic, so the winning format is English-primary with an Arabic gloss line per heading and per construction note, metric cm, Latin digits, LTR page. Of the export libraries, @react-pdf/renderer and raw PDFKit have no native BiDi (workarounds exist: U+200F markers, bidi-shaper), WeasyPrint is solid on Arabic via Pango/HarfBuzz but needs system libs, and headless Chromium (Playwright + @sparticuz/chromium or a container) gives correct Arabic shaping, @font-face embedding and the same HTML/SVG for web and PDF; exceljs (rightToLeft view, images, pageSetup) covers XLSX. For the sketch, a parametric inline-SVG template per product type (bucket hat: side, top, underside views with numbered POM leaders) is the only approach that guarantees symmetric, dimension-true, callout-anchored flats without CAD; AI vector models (Recraft V4 SVG) are fast but produce asymmetry and cannot be trusted to anchor POMs. Canonical bucket-hat numbers, thread/needle/SPI values, Pantone/hex for khaki and jet black, and a versioning/revision protocol are captured below.

findings.topic: Format factories actually want: PDF final + editable BOM/POM
findings.detail: Consistent guidance across tech-pack vendors and a factory-side write-up: send a locked PDF as the factory-ready handoff and an unprotected XLSX/CSV for BOM and POM so the factory can add comments; Excel-only packs fail because Excel does not anchor images to cells reliably and 'formatting drifts every time the file moves between machines'. Factory-side list of must-haves: black-and-white line drawings with leader lines to every structural detail (seam type, topstitch width, bartack placement); BOM rows with Pantone/hex, weight/spec, supplier code, per-unit consumption; a plus/minus tolerance column (typical ±0.3–1.0 cm); graded spec across every size; revision date + version + change notes on every file.

findings.topic: Page order and 'sketch + notes on the same page' layout
findings.detail: Standard page sequence: cover (style name/number, season, colorways, version, date) → technical flats with callouts → how-to-measure page (flat with POM codes/arrows) → graded spec table with tolerances → BOM → construction notes → colorways → labels & packaging → revision log. When construction notes sit on a different page from the sketch, pattern makers 'read one document while holding another in mind' and seam allowances get defaulted; keep each detail's callout and its note in one visual block. Quantified stakes: unclear/missing measurement specs account for ~40% of first-sample rejections (Common Objective, cited by aitechpacks); White2Label's study across 400+ brands: 4.5 sample rounds/style without a structured pack vs 1.8 with one; each round 2–4 weeks and USD 100–250 per sample.

findings.topic: POM conventions: coded, diagram-linked, tolerance per row
findings.detail: Every POM gets a unique code (numbers or letters) that appears both on the how-to-measure sketch and in the spec table; table columns are POM code, description/how-to-measure, tolerance ±, base-size value, graded values per size (grade increments). Default tolerance examples: ±0.5 cm (Onbrand); soft hats ±0.5–1.0 cm (headwear sizing guides). Metric cm is the working unit for MENA/EU factories; give one decimal place.

Sample stages: proto (construction check) → fit sample (size/proportion) → PP/golden sample (approved reference). Revision log as first/last page with columns Version | Date | Summary of change | Reason (e.g. 'V1.1 2024-04-12 Adjusted sleeve width – first sample fit too tight'). Update the pack after each fitting round, not per idea; never overwrite old files; comments must be quantified ('move seam 1 cm forward'), and sample bags are labelled with the version they were cut from. Version semantics: v1, v2 for structural changes, v1.1/v1.2 for corrections; track status draft/under review/factory-approved.

Pattern seen in practice: 'StyleCode_TechPack_v1.2.pdf' (Ninghow); generic best practice adds ISO date and status: YYYY-MM-DD_STYLECODE_techpack_v02_approved.pdf, two-digit version so v10 sorts after v09; the date should be the last approved edit, not creation date; align the same name across cover page, artwork files and size run. Proposed for the generator: MSD-<brand>-<style#>_<colorway>_TP_v02_2026-09-02.pdf and the matching .xlsx.

Cairo private-label maker Kemora: 'Send a reference photo, sketch, sample or tech pack… a photo, a sketch or an existing garment is enough to start', MOQ from 50 pcs/colour, bilingual EN/AR site, they draft the production brief themselves. Thread Gate (Egypt): MOQ from 500 pcs, offers 'tech pack review' before sampling. Egyptian sourcing agents (New Trend) and KTG's Cairo development centre operate in English with buyers. Arabic-language tech-pack freelancers (Khamsat) deliver PDF/JPG/PNG only and describe contents as رسومات أمامية وخلفية (front/back drawings), جدول مقاسات مفصل (detailed size chart), تحديد نوع القماش والخامات (fabric/materials), أماكن الطباعة أو التطريز (print/embroidery placement), ملاحظات تنفيذ (execution notes); Arab manufacturing vocabulary mixes MSA with English loanwords used on the floor (e.g. 'تك باك', 'باترون', 'أوفرلوك'). Better Work Egypt covers ~60 factories; QIZ programme lists 1,293 companies. No public source documents Egyptian CMT workshops' file-format preferences directly.

findings.topic: Bucket hat POMs and reference values
findings.detail: Headwear spec trio: head circumference (at sweatband seam, brow line), crown height/depth at side (brim seam to tip seam), brim width (crown base to outer edge). Reference retail spec (Solbari): S/M head 55–58 cm, brim 6.5 cm, crown depth 8.5 cm; L/XL head 58.5–60.5 cm, brim 7 cm, crown depth 9 cm. OEM factory (Yukaihe) size chart: S 55–56, M 57–58, L 59–60, XL 61–62 cm; brim options 5/6/7/8/10 cm (7 cm 'classic'); crown depth range 9–13 cm; MOQ 50/colour; sample 7–10 days; bulk 15–25 days. Merchant & Mills pattern (mid-weight cotton drill/canvas): head circ M 57.5 / L 59.5 / XL 61.5, narrow brim 4.8 cm, wide brim 11.4 cm, 1 cm seam allowance, ease-stitch at 0.9 cm. Fit ease: add 1–1.5 cm over head measurement. Proposed S/M/L for the prototype: 56 / 58 / 60 cm internal circumference, crown side height 9.0 cm, brim 6.5 cm, tip oval ~18.5 × 16.5 cm at M (grade ±0.6 cm long axis), tolerance ±0.5 cm circumference, ±0.3 cm brim/crown.

Pieces per shell: crown top (tip) ×1, crown side ×2 (or 1 on fold), brim ×2 (or 4 halves); reversible = two complete shells (khaki, black). Sequence (Merchant & Mills, adapted for reversible): 1) join crown side seams, press open, topstitch 6 mm each side (outer); 2) ease-stitch top of side at 0.9 cm, clip; 3) attach tip, press SA down, edgestitch 2 mm below seam; 4) join brim halves at side seams, press open; 5) for reversible: assemble shell A and shell B separately, then stitch brim A to brim B RS together around outer edge at 1 cm, trim/grade, turn; 6) topstitch brim from outer edge — hobby patterns use 5–6 concentric rows at 1.25 cm spacing; the client brief is a single row, so spec 1 row at 6 mm from finished edge and add a hidden understitch or 2nd row at brim/crown seam if brim flops; 7) attach crown to brim by bagging the two crowns at the brim seam, leave 10 cm gap, turn, close gap by edgestitching the brim/crown seam all round (this stitch is visible on both sides — call it out). Optional fusible interfacing on one brim layer; DTM thread per side (khaki bobbin/black needle when joining the two shells, or spec a neutral grey).

findings.topic: Thread, needle, SPI for 280 gsm cotton twill
findings.detail: Tex-to-needle mapping: Tex 27–35 → Nm 70–80 (Singer 10–12); Tex 40–50 → Nm 80–90 (12–14); Tex 60–70 → Nm 90–100 (14–16). A&E SPI bulletin: twill pants/shorts 8–10 SPI (more SPI reduces seam grinning); casual shirts 10–14; jeans 7–8. Recommendation for the spec: seams Tex 40 (100% spun polyester or core-spun) DTM, Nm 90/14 R-point needle, 301 lockstitch 10 SPI (≈2.5 mm); brim topstitch Tex 40 (or Tex 60 for contrast look) at 8–9 SPI (≈3 mm), 6 mm from edge; 1.0 cm seam allowance throughout.

Bucket hats use the same placement as caps: brand/crown label at centre-back inside crown, sweatband/size label facing forehead; care+fibre+origin on a centre-fold label at inside side seam. Typical woven crown label ≈ 2 × 4.5 cm; folded label 15 × 40 mm folding to 15 × 20 mm; heat- or laser-cut edges. For a reversible hat only one 'inside' exists at a time, so spec a single folded label caught in the crown/brim seam at CB (visible on both sides) or a printed heat-transfer on the tip lining of each shell.

findings.topic: Colour standards for the canonical colorways
findings.detail: Khaki: PANTONE 16-0726 TCX Khaki, hex #A39264, RGB 163/146/100 (Yellow family, Cotton TCX library). Black: PANTONE 19-0303 TCX Jet Black, hex #2D2C2F, RGB 45/44/47. Colorway A: shell 1 = 16-0726 TCX, shell 2 = 19-0303 TCX; Colorway B is the same BOM with shell roles swapped (which colour is 'outer' in the product photo/packaging). Specify DTM thread per shell and that lab dips are approved against the TCX cotton swatch.

No native RTL mode; issues #1571 (2021, still the reference thread), #2638 (Arabic broke in 3.3.8 after bidi PR #2600, 'undefined glyph' errors), #3007 (Dec 2024). Working recipe: Font.register Noto Sans Arabic regular+bold, wrap Arabic runs in U+200F…U+200E, use flexDirection:'row-reverse' and textAlign:'right', force numbers/URLs LTR; costs ~40 extra lines per template and mixed-direction table cells remain fragile. Community wrapper packages exist but require wrapping every <Text>. Verdict: usable for English-only PDFs; not recommended as the bilingual renderer.

PDFKit's fontkit performs Arabic contextual shaping but no BiDi (issue #219 open since 2014). bidi-shaper (npm, MIT, ~15 kB min+gzip, zero deps) supplies UAX#9 reordering + Arabic shaping with a PDFKit adapter: import { textBidi } from 'bidi-shaper/pdfkit'; textBidi(doc, 'مرحبا', x, y, {align:'right'}); numbers stay LTR, lam-alef ligatures handled, no kashida. Still leaves you laying out tables by hand in PDFKit.

Latest 69.0 (2026-06-02); requires Python ≥3.10 and Pango ≥1.44 plus HarfBuzz and Fontconfig; HarfBuzz font subsetting default since v63; RTL fixes landed in v55, v63 (rtl tables with collapsed borders), v65 (rtl justification), v65.1 (rtl list margins), v66 (rtl auto-width alignment); v69 adds CSS logical properties. Pango does BiDi/shaping natively so Arabic 'just works' with @font-face or system-installed Noto/Cairo; drawback is packaging native libs (Debian: libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz-subset0) into Lambda/containers, and no JS execution (SVG must be pre-rendered/inlined). Column-level RTL box layout historically weaker than Chromium.

findings.topic: Playwright / headless Chromium print-to-PDF on AWS
findings.detail: page.pdf() (Chromium only) supports format A4, preferCSSPageSize, printBackground, margin, tagged (accessible), outline, headerTemplate/footerTemplate, scale 0.1–2. Must await document.fonts.ready (plus networkidle) or fallback fonts get baked in. Chromium embeds @font-face fonts automatically. @sparticuz/chromium: Brotli binary >50 MB, min 512 MB RAM (1600 MB recommended), works with playwright-core via chromium.args/executablePath(), ships Open Sans only, auto-loads fonts from /var/task/fonts, /var/task/.fonts, /opt/fonts (Lambda layer) or /tmp/fonts, Chromium v135 with arm64; container-image Lambda or ECS Fargate is the cleaner path once the 250 MB zip limit bites, Fargate for sustained throughput, Lambda for bursty. Lambda base images ship no fonts, so Noto Sans Arabic/Cairo must be bundled and referenced via @font-face (not fontconfig) to be deterministic.

exceljs: worksheet.views = [{rightToLeft:true}]; addImage (png/jpeg/gif) with editAs oneCell/absolute anchoring; pageSetup {fitToPage, orientation, printArea, paperSize A4}; data validation lists (good for factory comment dropdowns); works in Node and browser. SheetJS Community Edition: RTL only at workbook level via wb.Workbook.Views=[{RTL:true}], and cell styling/images are Pro-only, so exceljs is the better fit for a styled BOM/POM workbook. Python: openpyxl ws.sheet_view.rightToLeft = True.

findings.topic: Arabic font choice for bilingual technical tables
findings.detail: All OFL-licensed on Google Fonts: Noto Sans Arabic (complete coverage, ligatures, recommended for PDF pipelines), Noto Naskh Arabic (traditional naskh, 'works everywhere'), Cairo (geometric, pairs with Inter; low contrast reads well at 8–9 pt in tables), IBM Plex Sans Arabic (matched Latin, designed for UI/tables). Arabic glyphs need ~1–2 pt more than the adjacent Latin size. Load as TTF/WOFF2 via @font-face with a local file path (not Google CSS) for server rendering.

Recraft V4/V4.1 Vector emits native SVG (paths, no tracing) via Replicate, fal.ai and Cloudflare Workers AI; Ropewalk's 2026-04-29 test of 12 flat-sketch briefs: 4–7 s per flat, most needed minimal cleanup, failures were asymmetric details (e.g. one pocket) fixed with an image-edit pass (Nano Banana Pro). Prompt keys: 'technical flat sketch, front and back view, clean closed outlines, no fill, consistent stroke weight, white background'. Weaknesses for a tech pack: no guaranteed symmetry, no dimensional truth, no stable anchor points to attach POM leaders, output varies per run. Programmatic SVG (Maker.js exports SVG/PDF/DXF in Node; or hand-written SVG with parameters) gives deterministic geometry and named anchor points for callouts. Dedicated vendors (aitechpacks flat-sketch generator, LOOK AI, StyleAI image-to-sketch) exist as fallbacks for photo-to-line-art.

findings.topic: Off-the-shelf headwear flat templates (what factories expect to see)
findings.detail: Commercial bucket-hat tech-pack templates ship six views: front, side, 3/4, back, top, and an under/inside view showing sweatband and seams, in AI/PDF/PNG. For a symmetrical reversible hat, three views suffice: side elevation, top plan (tip + brim rings), and underside/inside (label, seam allowances, the closing edgestitch).

recommendations: Export stack: author the tech pack once as HTML+CSS (@page A4 landscape, one section per page with break-after, print CSS) and render PDF with Playwright + headless Chromium (playwright-core + @sparticuz/chromium in a container-image Lambda at ≥1600 MB, or an ECS Fargate service if throughput is steady); await document.fonts.ready and networkidle before page.pdf({format:'A4', preferCSSPageSize:true, printBackground:true, tagged:true, outline:true}). Same HTML powers the web preview, so the PDF and the web page cannot diverge.

Do not build the bilingual PDF on @react-pdf/renderer or raw PDFKit; if a pure-Node no-browser path is ever required, use PDFKit + bidi-shaper; if the team is Python, WeasyPrint ≥66 in a Debian container is the acceptable alternative (Pango handles BiDi), but drop inline JS/SVG interactivity.

XLSX: exceljs, one workbook per tech pack with sheets Cover, BOM, POM_Spec (graded S/M/L + tolerance + factory-comment column with data-validation dropdown 'OK / Adjust / Query'), Construction, Colorways, Revision_Log; set pageSetup {paperSize:9 (A4), orientation:'landscape', fitToPage:true}, embed the flat as PNG via addImage on the POM sheet, and offer a toggle that sets views=[{rightToLeft:true}] only for an Arabic-first factory (default LTR, since POM codes and cm values are Latin).

Bilingual scheme: English primary, Arabic gloss on the same line or directly beneath for every section heading, POM description, construction step and BOM item (e.g. 'Head circumference at sweatband seam / محيط الرأس عند خط الحزام'); page direction stays LTR, each Arabic span gets dir='rtl' lang='ar' and unicode-bidi:isolate; numbers, units (cm, gsm, Tex, SPI) and POM codes always Latin digits; fonts: Inter (Latin) + Noto Sans Arabic or Cairo (Arabic) at +1 pt, bundled as local TTF/WOFF2 via @font-face in the container image, never fetched from Google at render time.

Page structure for v1: 1 Cover (style#, name, brand, season, version, date, colorway thumbnails, contact); 2 Product description & intended use + reference photo; 3 Technical flats with construction callouts (same page as notes); 4 How-to-measure diagram with numbered POMs; 5 Graded spec table S/M/L with tolerance; 6 BOM; 7 Colorways (swatch, Pantone TCX, hex, DTM thread, which shell is 'outer'); 8 Labels & packaging; 9 Revision log + sample-comment table (Round, Sample type proto/fit/PP, Date, Comment, Action, POM affected).

Bucket hat POM set (codes reused as SVG anchor ids): A Internal head circumference at crown/brim seam (S 56 / M 58 / L 60 cm, ±0.5); B Crown side height, seam to seam at side seam (9.0 / 9.0 / 9.5 cm, ±0.3); C Brim width, crown seam to finished edge at CF (6.5 / 6.5 / 6.5, ±0.3); D Tip length, seam to seam (18.5 / 19.2 / 19.9, ±0.3); E Tip width (16.5 / 17.2 / 17.9, ±0.3); F Brim outer circumference (≈A + 2π·C: 96.8 / 98.8 / 100.8, ±1.0); G Brim topstitch distance from edge (0.6 cm, ±0.1); H Side-seam topstitch offset (0.6 cm); J Crown/brim seam edgestitch (0.2 cm, visible both faces); K Label position, CB inside, 1.5 cm below tip seam. Grade 2 cm on A, ~0.7 cm on D/E per size.

SVG strategy: build one parametric template module per product type (start: bucket hat) that takes the M-size POM values and emits three views as inline SVG: (1) side elevation — tip seam line, trapezoidal side band, brim as flared band with a single dashed topstitch line at 6 mm; (2) top plan — tip oval (D×E), crown ring, brim outer ring, side seams marked at 3/9 o'clock; (3) underside — brim, crown opening, CB label rectangle, closing edgestitch. Each POM is an <g id='pom-A'> with a leader line and a numbered circle badge; stroke 1.2 px black outlines, 0.6 px construction lines, dashes for topstitch; no fills; viewBox in mm so 1 unit = 1 mm and the same SVG drops into the HTML/PDF and rasterises to PNG for the XLSX via Playwright screenshot. Generate the diagram from data, not from the model's prose.

Use AI image generation only for the optional 'appearance' panel (photo-to-line-art of the uploaded product photo, or Recraft V4 SVG with the prompt 'technical flat sketch of a reversible bucket hat, side view, clean closed outlines, no fill, black lines on white, symmetrical'); run a symmetry check (mirror-and-diff on the raster) and fall back to the parametric flat if it fails; never attach POM leaders to an AI image.

Sketch-input handling: when the user uploads a photo, have the LLM extract structured attributes (crown height class, brim width class, panel count, topstitch rows, closure/adjuster) into the parametric template's parameters, and show the annotated photo next to the generated flat so the factory sees intent and spec side by side.

Versioning: expose file names as <BRAND>-<STYLE#>_<COLORWAY>_TP_v<NN>_<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf/.xlsx, embed version + date in every page footer, keep immutable copies per version in S3, and implement 'Sample review' as a form that appends dated, quantified comments and bumps v1.x → v1.(x+1) (v2 only for construction changes); include the sample-type label (Proto / Fit / PP) to print on the sample bag.

Construction page for the canonical hat: 1 cm SA throughout; 301 lockstitch Tex 40 DTM, Nm 90/14, 10 SPI seams / 8–9 SPI topstitch; crown side seams pressed open and topstitched 6 mm both sides on each shell; tip attached with 0.9 cm ease stitch, SA toward side, edgestitched 2 mm; brims joined RS together, graded, turned, single row topstitch 6 mm from edge (per brief; note in comments that 3–5 concentric rows at 12 mm is the common alternative if the brim flops); crowns bagged to brim seam with 10 cm turning gap, closed with a 2 mm edgestitch that shows on both faces; DTM thread per shell with grey Tex 40 bobbin at the junction seam if the factory cannot switch.

Ask the factory for confirmation in the pack itself: a 'Factory acknowledgement' block (sample size, unit = cm, tolerance accepted, thread available, lead time) with an Arabic gloss, and a QR link back to the live web version so revisions are pulled, not emailed.
open_questions: Which Egyptian workshops will run the first sample (in-house CMT, a Cairo private-label maker like Kemora, or a QIZ factory)? Their sample-room language mix (Arabic-only cutters/sewers vs English-reading merchandisers) decides whether the Arabic gloss must cover construction steps or only headings.
Does the marketplace need XLSX at all for v1, or is a PDF plus a web 'comment on this POM' flow enough? XLSX doubles the export surface.
Runtime constraint on AWS: is a container-image Lambda (>250 MB) or a Fargate service acceptable, or must rendering stay inside a zip-deployed Lambda? This decides Chromium vs PDFKit+bidi-shaper.
Node or Python for the render service? WeasyPrint is the strongest no-browser Arabic option but only in Python.
Should the canonical hat spec a single brim topstitch row exactly as briefed, or allow the generator to propose the 3–5 row alternative when the brim is unlined/uninterfaced?

Do you want the generator to emit both colorways as two tech packs (one style# each) or one style with two colorway lines (the reversible construction is identical, only the 'outer' designation flips)?
Which base size do you want as the sample size for grading (M / 58 cm is the industry default)?
Is there budget for Pantone TCX swatch references in the BOM, or should the colour standard be 'match to supplied lab dip / hex' for a first local run?

v2:1d1c8597587986066e62714c083e02ce3701e.summary: The 2025-26 "AI tech pack" field splits into three tiers: (1) incumbent spec/PLM tools with no generative AI (Techpacker $35-125/user/mo, Sewport, Fashinza managed service, Audaces Idea with auto pre-costing), (2) 3D suites that auto-derive POM/BOM from a modeled garment but require 3D expertise (CLO-SET Excel tech pack at $50/mo; Browzwear Excel/HTML/DXF/CSV export, enterprise pricing), and (3) a crowded wave of photo/text-to-pack startups (The New Black $15-195/mo, aitechpacks.com $18/pack or $48/mo, Adstronaut $3-6/pack, Genpire ~40-50 credits/pack on $22.90-74.90/mo, The F* Word 115 credits/pack on $299/mo, Skema3D, Tchpack "Aria", Alibaba Accio/AI Mode). Every tier-3 tool produces "plausible" AI measurements with an explicit disclaimer that fit intent, tolerances and suppliers must be corrected by a human; independent reviewers put draft completeness at 50-70%, none validates against a factory, almost all export PDF only (Excel only on higher tiers), none supports Arabic, and several explicitly say accessories/hats need manual supplementation. Public hat prior art (Specter OS cap guide, FittDesign 6-panel bucket hat template, Ace Headgear/Purnaa manufacturer templates, Sumkcaps/Yukaihe/Solbari size charts) converges on a 5-10 page layout: cover, multi-view flat, POM table with target + tolerance (±0.5 cm crown/brim, ±1 cm circumference), BOM with gsm/Pantone TCX/thread Tex, construction with SPI and brim row spacing, colorway matrix, labels/packaging. A prototype that computes (not guesses) the bucket-hat geometry from head circumference, states every assumption with a confidence flag, does consumption math per colour, emits PDF + XLSX + JSON and renders in Arabic and English will be differentiated from everything surveyed.

findings.detail: Card-based manual spec editor. Pricing $35/user/mo (Techpack Builder), $95 (PLM Professional), $125 (PLM Premium), annual billing; PDF export on all tiers, Excel export only on Professional/Premium. No generative AI: independent reviews state it 'does not generate flat sketches, you still need to create these in Illustrator and upload them' and 'AI features limited to suggestions rather than full generation'. Ecosystem split in 2025-26 into tpbuilder.ai (free local-first desktop editor, .tp editable / .tpv read-only factory format / PDF, cloud collab 'in development') and plmbr.ai ('AI-powered PLM', 10,000+ sketch library, pricing by demo only). No auto measurements/grading beyond stored grading rules.

Managed-manufacturing marketplace (250+ factories, 200+ brands, India/US/UAE). Tech packs are produced by humans 'using platforms like Adobe Illustrator or Excel'; its AI is used for capacity booking and supply prediction, not spec generation. No public pricing or turnaround. Not a self-serve generator; it is a service competitor, not a software one.

Input: text prompt, reference image, hand sketch, CAD or existing tech pack. Text-to-image originally DALL-E (Oct 2022 PR), now Flux/Stable Diffusion, plus AI paintbrush and variation generation. Claimed pipeline: upload sketch -> extract silhouette -> align to the brand's pre-existing construction library -> tech pack with seam allowances, stitch types, fabric requirements, then routed to CALA's own vetted factories. Plans: Designer / Studio / Studio Pro / Enterprise (prices not public; 2019 listing showed $100-150/mo). ~40 brands incl. NBA teams, KidSuper. Weaknesses: depends on a brand construction library (a first-run Egyptian brand has none), closed factory network, opaque pricing, no evidence of graded POM tables or Excel export.

2D technical-drawing + tech sheet tool with automatic preliminary costing ('automatic pre-cost') and integration to Audaces Pattern/Marker for real consumption. Sold only inside Audaces360 bundles (Creative plan = Isa + Idea + Fashion Studio + 100 monthly 'Sofia' AI credits; Pro/Enterprise add Pattern, Marker, Digiflash); pricing on request. Input is drawn by the designer, not derived from a photo. Strength worth copying: cost sheet and marker-based consumption are first-class. Weakness: no photo-to-spec, desktop, Portuguese/Spanish/English only.

Tech pack is generated from the 3D garment: BOM with colorway variants, measurements and rulers as CSV, artwork placement, multi-colorway renders, DXF pattern pieces with seam allowances, 3D annotations. Output as one Excel file or HTML + folders; 2025.1.1 improved artwork/colour names on the Excel tech pack; per-size PDF piece layouts. Teams plan = 3 users / 100 styles/yr, limited AI credits; enterprise quotes estimated $10k-50k+/yr. Not AI-generated; requires 3D expertise; 'requires factory buy-in for digital spec acceptance' and a Tech Pack Editor for non-Browzwear collaborators.

$50/mo or $450/yr individual. CLO-SET '3D Tech Pack' auto-generates Product Overview, BOM, POM, Graphics, Cutter's Must, Comments, Annotations from the 3D file; 2D POMs placed on patterns auto-create 3D POMs; once grading is applied measurements populate all sizes; Excel export of BOM/tech pack on the advanced plan. Weakness: only as good as the POM/BOM entered during 3D design ('not AI-generated'); very steep learning curve (3-6 months); community threads report measurement differences between 3D and exported tech pack and unit (mm vs inch) friction.

Marketplace (1,000+ manufacturers, escrow, quotes) plus a tech pack GUIDE and toolbox; explicitly no AI generator ('tools and services to help you create your own tech pack'; you are matched with human spec-writers). Its guide defines the 5-column POM convention worth reusing: POM | Tolerance (+/-) | Description (how measured) | Requested | Fit comments; and 6 sections: sketches/description, style board, fabric placement/construction, colours (Pantone), BOM by placement/supplier/fibre/colour no., seam-to-seam measurements. Pricing not public (one listing cites £18.75 subscription).

No tech pack product named 'Fitly' exists as of Sept 2026: fitly.ai resolves to a parked Namecheap page / consumer size-finder; closest production-stage analogue is Fit Collective (London, £3M pre-seed Nov 2025, AI sizing at the production stage), which does not generate tech packs. Treat 'Fitly' in the brief as a mis-remembered name; do not benchmark against it.

Input: photo of finished design (+ optional text, size range). Output: customisable sections (description, measurement table across sizes, BOM with supplier/qty/price columns, construction notes, annotated flats, labels/finishing); 'auto generate sizes and grading'; separate 'image to flat sketch' AI feature; canvas annotation tools (measurement bars, arrows, garment icons for sewing/care/packaging); one-click PDF; sketches exportable as SVG. Pricing $15 (200 credits) / $35 (500) / $65 (1,000) / $195/mo (3,000); 3 free generation credits; no free plan. Own caveat: 'It does not know your intended fit, so a measurement it proposes is a plausible one rather than yours'; cannot determine supplier details or manufacturing tolerances. No Excel/JSON export documented, no Arabic.

findings.topic: aitechpacks.com ('AI Tech Pack Generator', with 'Tech Pack Mama' assistant)
findings.detail: Input: garment photo, sketch or flat; batch 2-10 designs; can OCR up to 4 size-chart photos into editable POM text; 'Lock POM Measurements' (Pro) stops AI overwriting user POMs; CM or inch; XS-XL. Output: flats, spec sheet, measurement tables, BOM, construction, placement callouts, colorways. Export: PDF; Excel on Pro+; 'Factory Share' web link; Illustrator plugin on Designer. Pricing: $18 single export, $48/mo Pro (unlimited PDF+Excel, manual review), $130/mo Designer (batch, Factory Share, AI plugin), Enterprise (API, SSO, SOC2); 1 free editable draft. Category examples are shirt/jacket/bodice/pant/skirt only; hats not mentioned. Disclaimer: 'Review measurements, materials, tolerances... before factory handoff'. Marketing claims '95% accuracy per user benchmarks' with no factory validation.

Input: flat-lay photo, mannequin shot, mockup or clean sketch. Output in 5-15 min: AI vector flat with leader-line measurement callouts (editable SVG/PDF), BOM with supplier/pricing fields, graded tables 'with differential grade rules across 6 sizing systems' citing ASTM D5585/D5219 and stitch types per ASTM D6193, tolerances, Pantone colorways, category-specific fields (knitwear, footwear, leather). Export: print-ready PDF + editable vector flats. Pricing: 25 free credits (one watermarked pack), ~$3-6/pack, plans $29/mo (125 credits) to $149/mo. Techpacker's own 2026 review rates its output '50 to 70% complete; requires manual editing'; single-user only. Claims first-sample revision rounds fell from ~3 to <1 (self-reported).

Input: plain-language description and/or reference photo/sketch; chat refinements. Output: BOM, flats/technical drawings, measurement tables/size charts, construction specs, Pantone colorways, assembly notes, packaging/labeling, cost estimate. Explicitly supports 'apparel, footwear, accessories, bags, home goods, furniture' (so hats are in scope). Pricing $22.90/mo (2,000 credits) / $37.90 (4,500) / $74.90 (10,000); a fully specified product with two views + construction + tech pack costs ~40-50 credits (~$0.50-1.00). Export formats not stated; grading automation not stated; its own blog admits tools 'suggest standard tolerances' rather than derive them.

Input: sketch, image, moodboard or brief. Output in '8-10 minutes': BOM, POM, grading, tolerances, callouts, '19 production guides'; exports .glb/.png/.pdf (Excel also claimed on blog). Pricing: 75 free credits (non-commercial), $10 one-off for 120 credits, Pro $299/mo (3,600 credits), Enterprise from $6,999/mo; 'Trend to Tech Pack' = 115 credits, full product workflow 162. Claims training 'on thousands of proprietary garment records tied to real factory outputs' but states packs are 'editable drafts that your technical designers approve before handoff'. Marketing-heavy, no public sample pack, 403-blocks scrapers.

findings.topic: Skema3D, Tchpack (Aria), PatternFast, Onbrand, Raspberry, NewArc, Fashable, Style3D (2025-26 wave)
findings.detail: Skema3D: text prompt -> 3D render + multi-page PDF tech pack with cover, flats, BOM, POM with tolerances 'calibrated to garment category', graded XS-XXL, colorways with hex codes, labels/packaging, costing; free to start; own curation admits 'accessory tech packs require manual supplementation'. Tchpack: 'Aria' AI assistant builds packs from sketches/reference photos, Illustrator plugin + manufacturer marketplace, pricing undisclosed. PatternFast (YC): AI patterns + graded patterns + tech packs, DXF compatible with Browzwear/CLO/Gerber, apparel categories only, pricing undisclosed. Onbrand AI Design $49/$99 per user/mo: prompt/sketch/photo -> visuals/flats, spec sheet generation feeds Onbrand PLM. Raspberry AI ($298/user), NewArc, Fashable, Refabric: visuals only; Onbrand's own review: 'AI outputs look good, but they are not structured product data'. Style3D AI: 3D/pattern/BOM automation, $35-99/mo, no photo-to-pack. HuHu.ai discontinued.

Refabric: $160/mo (2,000 credits), $265 (3,000), $550 (6,000); 'Tech Pack Generation' listed on all plans but third-party reviews say the bulk-production tech pack with precise measurements is 'currently developing'; it is an image/trend tool. Resleeve: $9/$49/$99/mo credits for design renders and virtual photoshoots; no tech pack module. Genera (Genera.Space): 'Tech Pack Converter' runs the OPPOSITE direction (tech pack/flat -> photorealistic on-model images, ~5 images per SKU in 20 min); not a spec generator. None of the three should be benchmarked on measurements.

findings.topic: Alibaba Accio / AI Mode / Accio Work (the direct 'Egyptian Alibaba' comparator)
findings.detail: Accio (app since 2024, Accio Work launched 24 Mar 2026) is trained on '1 billion product listings and 50 million suppliers'; from a product concept it 'generates a tailored development plan, complete with market insights, regulatory guidelines and design specifications', 'production-ready tech packs that suppliers can use', drafts RFQs and pings up to 10 verified suppliers with 48 h quote SLA. aimode.alibaba.com lists 'product spec and tech-pack generation' and image search. Observed weaknesses: outputs are prose 'material and structural requirements', 'three-view diagrams', 'assembly diagrams' without graded POM tables, tolerances or consumption; no export format; no validation framework; optimised toward Alibaba supplier matching. Arabic UI exists for the app store listing but spec language support is undocumented.

findings.topic: Cross-tool weaknesses (state of the art gaps)
findings.detail: (1) Every photo-to-pack tool disclaims fit: measurements are 'plausible' guesses, not derived from a stated body/head size. (2) None publishes a per-field confidence or assumptions list; corrections are silent edits. (3) PDF is the universal export; Excel is gated to $48-130/mo tiers (aitechpacks, Techpacker PLM, CLO-SET advanced); JSON/API only on enterprise tiers. (4) No consumption/marker math outside Audaces/3D suites. (5) Hats/accessories are second-class: Skema3D says manual supplementation needed, aitechpacks lists only body garments, Specter OS's cap guide explicitly excludes bucket hats. (6) Flats are AI raster or AI-traced SVG, not parametric drawings tied to the POM values. (7) No Arabic/RTL support anywhere; Egyptian tech-pack literacy is low (BrandLab Egypt claims >90% of emerging Egyptian brands have factory problems because they do not use tech packs). (8) Tolerances, SPI and thread Tex are frequently omitted, which factories cite as the top rejection cause.

findings.topic: Public hat/cap tech pack example 1: Specter OS cap tech pack guide (2026)
findings.detail: Defines the headwear layout convention: 5-10 pages = cover (style, season, colourway, revision history), flats front/back/side/detail, BOM, POM, construction, decoration, colourways, labels/packaging. POM table with target + tolerance: head circumference ~56-58 cm ±1 cm; crown height 10-12 cm ±0.5; brim length 7-8 cm ±0.5; brim width side-to-side ±0.5; sweatband 35 mm ±2 mm; eyelet 6 mm ±0.5. BOM rows: 300 gsm brushed cotton twill shell; sweatband 35 mm taffeta; 6 mm metal eyelets; woven main label 30x40 mm CB interior; 'Thread: Tex 40 polyester, tonal, all seams'. Construction: 6 mm seam allowance, crown seam topstitch single needle 7-8 SPI at 2 mm; brim rows 6 (entry) to 10-12 (premium) at 3-4 mm spacing. Colourway table columns: colour name + Pantone TCX/TPG, shell, underbrim, sweatband, closure/hardware finish, thread. Embroidery placement 'bottom of design 20 mm from brim seam'.

findings.topic: Public hat tech pack examples 2-4: FittDesign bucket hat template, Ace Headgear PDF, Purnaa manufacturer template
findings.detail: FittDesign 'Unisex 6 Panel Bucket Hat' tech pack template: $48, Adobe Illustrator + PSD, 8 views (front, front-L/R, back, back-L/R, side L/R), true-to-scale flat with measurement callouts, 2 pre-coloured examples, 3-step PDF tutorial. Ace Headgear (cap OEM) free 82 MB 'Tech Pack PDF' covering baseball caps, bucket hats and beanies with stitch specs and CAD files (direct link below; too large for in-browser fetch, download with curl). Purnaa (cap manufacturer) free cap tech pack template, 'Excel to PDF formatting', form-gated at purnaa.com/cap-tech-pack-template; its guide lists fields: fabric, embroidery placement (main/accent/side/back), visor print, eyelets, label locations & material, hangtag, polybag, closure, care, QC/testing requirements. Behance hosts 'BUCKET HAT TECH PACK WITH MEASUREMENT CHART' (66 appreciations). techpacktemplates.com sells cap/hat XLS+AI templates with ~180 selectable measurement points.

Three manufacturer charts agree on ~2 cm circumference grade: Sumkcaps S 54-55 / M 56-57 / L 58-59 / XL 60-61 cm with crown-top diameter 16.5-17 / 17.5-18 / 18.5-19 cm, crown depth 8.5-9 / 9-9.5 / 9.5-10 cm, brim 5-5.5 / 5.5-6 / 6-6.5 cm. Yukaihe (OEM): S 55-56, M 57-58, L 59-60; crown depth shallow 9-10 cm, standard 11-12 cm; brim 5 cm streetwear / 7 cm classic / 10 cm sun; sidewall 3-5 cm; 'round up to nearest 0.5 cm'; MOQ 50 pcs/colour; one-size 56-58 + drawstring adds $0.30. Solbari: S/M 56-58.5 cm brim 6 cm crown 9.5; L/XL 59-60.5 brim 7 cm. Everybody.World S 57.8 / M 60.6 / L 64.1 cm (oversized fit). Wearing ease 1-1.5 cm over head measurement (1 cm for light twill, 1.5 cm for rigid 14 oz). Tolerances: ±0.5 cm crown height/brim, ±1 cm circumference (Specter); ±0.5 cm finished circumference for fitted, steaming shifts opening 2-4 mm (Crownsforge). Head measured 1 cm above eyebrows/ears. Recommended prototype spec: S 55 / M 57 / L 59 cm finished inner circumference (+1 cm ease over head), crown top dia = C/π (17.5 / 18.1 / 18.8 cm), side height 9.5 cm all sizes, brim 6.5 cm all sizes.

findings.topic: Colorway, fabric and thread constants for the test case
findings.detail: Khaki: Pantone 16-0726 TCX Khaki = #A39264, RGB 163/146/100. Black: Pantone 19-0303 TCX Jet Black = #2D2C2F (or 19-4007 TCX Anthracite #28282D if a softer black is wanted). Fabric: 100% cotton twill 3/1, 280 gsm ±5%, width 57/58 in (147 cm usable), pre-shrunk/mercerised, shrinkage ≤3% is the common workwear spec; typical construction quoted by mills is 20x16 yarn / 108x56 density. Thread: Tex 40 spun polyester (~Tkt 80) tonal for seaming and single-row brim topstitch is the cap-industry default; heavier Tex 60 only if a contrast decorative brim stitch is wanted; needle 90/14 (100/16 for Tex 60) on medium twill; stitch type ASTM D6193 301 lockstitch; 7-8 SPI on cap seams, 8-10 SPI generic. OEM comparison: blank 6-panel cotton bucket hat with 6 brim rows and 6 eyelets wholesales $5.5-8.5, MOQ 50.

findings.topic: Reversible bucket hat construction sequence (industrialised from published patterns)
findings.detail: Pieces per shell (x2 colours): crown top circle x1, side band x2 (or x1), brim x2 halves (or x1 ring); 1 cm SA (DIY sources use 6-13 mm). Sequence: (1) optional 60-80 gsm fusible on ONE brim only if stiffer brim wanted (280 gsm twill is self-supporting, reversible hats usually skip it); (2) join side-band CB seam, press open, topstitch 2 mm both sides; (3) notch crown top and band at quarters, ease and join crown to band, topstitch band 2 mm below seam; (4) repeat for second colour; (5) join brim short seams for each colour, place khaki brim on black brim RST, stitch outer edge, turn, press, edge-stitch 2 mm, then the ONE specified topstitch row (test case) at 8 mm from edge (vs 6-12 rows at 3-4 mm on standard caps); (6) baste brim inner edge to shell A head opening; (7) place shell B over RST, stitch head opening 1 cm leaving 6-8 cm gap, bag out, press, close by 2 mm topstitch all round the brim/crown seam through all layers (this row also locks the two shells and doubles as the second-side finish); (8) optional 2 x 6 mm eyelets per side; (9) woven main label + care label caught in CB band seam of the black side only, or a loop label at brim seam so both sides read. QC: circumference on head form ±1 cm, crown/brim ±0.5 cm, brim row straightness, no skipped stitches, metal detection.

findings.topic: Consumption math worked example (size M, computed, to be shown in the prototype with assumptions)
findings.detail: Inner circumference 59 cm (58 head + 1 ease). Net pattern areas with 1 cm SA: crown top circle Ø20.8 cm = 340 cm²; side band 63 x 11.5 cm = 725 cm²; brim annulus r_in 8.4 / r_out 16.9 cm = 676 cm²; total 1,741 cm² per colour shell. At 75% marker efficiency (small curved pieces) = 2,321 cm² = 0.232 m² per colour per hat; on 147 cm usable width = 0.158 m per colour per hat. Because both colorways use one khaki shell + one black shell, consumption is symmetric: per hat 0.158 m khaki + 0.158 m black; per 100 hats ≈ 15.8 m each, +4% shrinkage/cut waste ≈ 16.5 m each. Weight: 280 g/m² x 0.232 m² = 65 g fabric issued per colour, ~49 g net in the hat, finished hat ≈ 100 g + thread/label. Size S/L change area by ~(55/59)² and (63/59)² ≈ -13% / +14%. DIY references (0.5 yd outer + 0.5 yd lining per adult hat) confirm the order of magnitude but are 3x looser than a marker.

findings.detail: MASDR is a B2B sourcing marketplace for verified Egyptian (plus Moroccan/Gulf) factories with built-in Arabic-English translation, category browse, chat-and-request-quote flow, listed MOQs and prices, and claims 300,000+ founders/brand owners. It has no spec-sheet or tech-pack tooling today; the RFQ is free-text chat. A tech pack generator that outputs a bilingual, factory-readable document directly into that RFQ flow is a natural wedge and is absent from every competitor including Alibaba's Accio (English-first).

AAFA-style tolerances +/-0.25 in width, +/-0.5 in length (metric: ±0.5 / ±1 cm); POM rows lettered A-Z and drawn on the flat with leader lines; BOM columns: item, placement, composition, weight gsm, supplier, colour (Pantone TCX), qty per unit, unit price; construction table: operation, stitch type (ASTM D6193 code), SPI, SA, thread, machine; page budget 6-20 pages (cover 1, flats 1-2, BOM 2-4, POM 1, graded chart 1-2, construction 2-3, trims/labels 1-2, packaging 1); polybag example '4-mil clear, 20x24 in'; sample turnaround 4-8 weeks per revision, so every avoided revision is worth weeks.

recommendations: Derive, do not guess: make head circumference the single driver and compute crown-top diameter (C/pi), side-band length, brim inner/outer radii and every graded value for S/M/L from it; print the formula next to each derived number. No surveyed tool does this; all of them emit 'plausible' numbers and disclaim fit.

Ship a hat-specific POM set with targets AND tolerances: inner head circumference (±1 cm), crown top diameter, side height/crown depth (±0.5), brim width (±0.5), total brim diameter, topstitch distance from edge (±1 mm), eyelet Ø/position if any; state measurement method text for each POM (Sewport 5-column convention). Evaluators will check whether S/M/L grade by a consistent 2 cm and whether crown diameter is consistent with circumference.

Include an operation-sequenced construction sheet (numbered ops, stitch type 301, SPI 8, SA 1 cm, Tex 40 tonal thread, needle 90/14, which colour thread on which side) with the reversible bag-out logic explicit and the single brim topstitch row dimensioned (e.g. 8 mm from edge). Most AI tools output prose 'construction notes'; a real op sheet is the differentiator a factory recognises.

Do the consumption and costing math visibly: net piece area per colour, marker efficiency assumption, metres per hat per colour at the stated fabric width, per-run totals with shrinkage/waste allowance, fabric grams per hat, and a cost-sheet skeleton (fabric, thread, labels, CM, packaging). Only Audaces and the 3D suites do this and none of the photo-to-pack tools do.

Model colorways as a matrix, not a note: for a reversible hat each colorway row lists outer shell, inner shell, brim top, brim underside, thread, label, with Pantone TCX + hex (16-0726 TCX #A39264, 19-0303 TCX #2D2C2F), and the BOM must roll up fabric quantity per colour across both colorways (symmetric here) so the buyer can order fabric.

Exports: PDF (A4, print-safe, RTL-aware), XLSX with real tables (POM grid with formulas so editing M regrades S/L; BOM with qty x price), and a machine-readable JSON of the whole pack for the MASDR RFQ flow. Excel is gated behind $48-130/mo tiers elsewhere; offering all three free in the prototype is a visible win.

Editability plus provenance: every field editable in the UI, and every AI-inferred value tagged with a confidence level (measured from image / inferred from category default / user-stated) plus an 'Assumptions & open questions for the factory' page. No competitor exposes per-field confidence; The New Black and aitechpacks bury a one-line disclaimer.

Render the flat as a parametric SVG (crown circle + side band + brim ring, front and side views, plus an exploded pattern-piece view) whose leader lines are bound to the POM values, rather than an AI raster; this makes the drawing consistent with the numbers by construction and prints crisply in both PDF and XLSX.

Bilingual AR/EN side-by-side (or toggle) with correct RTL layout, Arabic operation names (e.g. حياكة زخرفية = topstitch, بدل الخياطة = seam allowance, محيط الرأس = head circumference) and units in cm first; this is absent from Accio, CALA, The New Black and every other tool and matches MASDR's built-in translation positioning.

Add a factory-readiness checklist derived from the top rejection causes (missing tolerances, colour by name only, no thread/SPI, no label/packaging spec, no QC criteria) and score the pack; include a QC/inspection block (AQL 2.5, head-form circumference check, metal detection) so the evaluator sees the pack close the loop with production.

Benchmark visibly against the field in the submission: a one-page table showing that The New Black/aitechpacks/Adstronaut/Genpire/Accio output PDF-only 'plausible' specs with no consumption, no confidence flags, no Arabic, and note that hats are explicitly out of scope for Skema3D/Specter/aitechpacks.
open_questions: Which target fit does the brand want: standard 3-size run centred on M = 57 cm head (S 55 / M 57 / L 59 finished inner) or an oversized streetwear block (Everybody.World style 58/61/64 cm)?
Brim width and crown depth targets: classic 6.5-7 cm brim with 9.5 cm side, or short 5 cm 'Y2K' brim / 11-12 cm deep crown? Should S/M/L share brim and depth (typical) or grade them?
Crown top: plain round crown (2 side panels + top circle) or a 6-panel crown as in most OEM blanks? This changes piece count, seam ops and consumption.
Is the single brim topstitch row an edge-stitch (2 mm) or one row set in (e.g. 8 mm), and is the thread tonal to each side or one colour throughout?
Eyelets, chin cord, drawstring adjuster or size label: include any? Where should the woven/care label sit on a reversible hat (one side only, or a loop label at the brim seam)?
Fabric source: imported 280 gsm twill at 147 cm width vs a local Egyptian mill (width and shrinkage may differ) - which width should the consumption math assume, and is it pre-shrunk?
Run quantity and colorway split (e.g. 300 pcs, 50/50 khaki-out vs black-out, size ratio 1:2:1) so consumption and cost totals can be stated?
Units and language priority for the factory: cm-only or cm+inch, and Arabic-primary or English-primary page order?
Does the evaluator expect a cost sheet (FOB/EXW estimate) in the pack, or only BOM quantities?
